Sin embargo, antes de pensar tan a largo plazo, los de Hansi Flick necesitan poner fin a una sangría defensiva que se prolonga lejos de casa. En la anterior jornada europea, frente al Aston Villa, el equipo azulgrana consiguió cerrar su portería por primera vez en la competición desde la ida de los cuartos de final contra el Borussia Dortmund en la temporada 2024-25. Un dato que demuestra que el problema no es nuevo y que el equipo necesita recuperar la solidez que le permita competir con garantías en las eliminatorias. Mantener la portería a cero es una de las grandes tareas pendientes para un conjunto que aspira a llegar hasta el final. La situación resulta todavía más llamativa cuando juega lejos de Barcelona. Para encontrar la última ocasión en la que el conjunto catalán no encajó un gol como visitante en la Champions League hay que remontarse a la ida de los octavos de final contra el Benfica, también en la campaña 2024-25. Desde entonces, el equipo ha disputado 12 encuentros europeos a domicilio y ha recibido al menos un tanto en todos ellos. Una dinámica que Joan García y la defensa azulgrana tratarán de romper cuanto antes. El próximo compromiso, ante el Sabah en Azerbaiyán, aparece como una oportunidad para cambiar esta tendencia. El escenario es propicio para que el Barcelona recupere la confianza defensiva y consiga, por fin, echar el cerrojo a su portería lejos del Camp Nou. El Barcelona tiene ante sí una oportunidad para demostrar que puede ser candidato a todo sin necesidad de convertir cada partido en un intercambio de golpes. La calidad ofensiva del equipo está fuera de toda duda, pero la solidez atrás será determinante cuando lleguen los cruces decisivos. Las apuestas deportivas ya reflejan la confianza en sus opciones de conquistar el título... aunque el primer paso pasa por dejar atrás una racha de 12 salidas europeas encajando. articles.title: Premier League: Why are there 12pm and 2:05pm kick-offs on Sunday?
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team explain why the Premier League fixtures have some unusual kick-off times this weekend.
articles.body:
The Premier League kick-off times look a little unusual this weekend, with no Saturday 12:30 GMT slot, and games starting at 12:00 and 14:05 on Sunday.

Everton will host local rivals Liverpool on Sunday at 12 noon because the match has been selected for live broadcast by TNT, who have a mid-day broadcast slot on that day. The game was originally scheduled for Saturday.

This has had a knock-on effect on the remaining fixtures.

On a typical Premier League weekend, the first matches will begin at 14:00 followed by a final 16:30 kick-off.

Pushing start times back five minutes to 14:05 reduces the risk of overlap with the unusual early 12:00 start time, while avoiding clashing with the 16:30 fixture.

Midweek European games have also affected the schedule, as the Premier League aims to prevent clubs from playing two matches within 60 hours of each other.

Crystal Palace , Sunderland , Bournemouth and Brighton are all set to play in the Europa and Conference Leagues on Thursday, ruling them out of Saturday Premier League fixtures.

articles.title: Arteta se 'Saka' un nuevo 'cañón': "Se fue y se convirtió en un Madueke diferente"
articles.standfirst: El extremo suma cuatro goles y tres asistencias en sus últimos 11 partidos con el Arsenal
articles.summary: El extremo suma cuatro goles y tres asistencias en sus últimos 11 partidos con el Arsenal
articles.body: Las r epetidas ausencias por lesión de Bukayo Saka han obligado a Mikel Arteta a buscar recambios de garantías y esta temporada ninguno le está funcionando tan bien como Noni Madueke (Londres, 2002). El ex de PSV y Chelsea, fichado hace un año a cambio de 56 millones de euros, ha dado un importante paso al frente. A sus explosivas conducciones comienza a sumar capacidad productiva: en los últimos 11 partidos que ha disputado, alternando izquierda y derecha, acumula cuatro goles y tres asistencias. Siendo, además, decisivo. Marcó el gol de la victoria ante el Nottingham Forest (0-1), logró el empate 'in extremis' en Newcastle (2-2), asistió a Martin Odegaard en el triunfo frente al Hull City (1-0), abrió la lata en la victoria por la mínima ante el Slavia (1-2)... y encontró a Viktor Gyökeres para que, con un tremendo 'zapatazo', estrenara el marcador ante el Borussia Dortmund (1-1). Una mejoría, unida a las marchas de Leandro Trossard y Gabriel Martinelli, que le ha permitido adelantar a Eberechi Eze en la rotación y pasar de ser la temporada pasada el 14º jugador con más minutos... a convertirse en el 8º. Su ausencia en las listas de Thomas Tuchel desde el Mundial le ayudó a abrir los ojos. "Lo que ha hecho es subir el nivel y en los entrenamientos ha sido el mejor jugador en los últimos diez días. No me dejó otra opción que hacerlo jugar. Se notaba que cada vez que estaba cerca del balón representaba una amenaza", certifica Arteta. "Es un Noni diferente", insiste el técnico 'gunner', que sólo le alineó de titular en dos de los primeros siete partidos del curso: "Su reacción es un gran ejemplo para el resto del equipo. Se fue, empezó a entrenar y se convirtió en un Noni diferente. No iba a aceptar esa situación, iba en serio y, desde entonces, ha sido increíble." "Le da igual jugar por la izquierda o por la derecha, pero ahora está mostrando algo más: otro nivel de garra, otro nivel de convicción... Se está volviendo decisivo en los partidos, que es lo que esperamos de un jugador como él. Y sí, también me encanta su intensidad sin balón. Se está convirtiendo en un jugador mucho más completo y creo que lo está disfrutando", insiste Arteta. Una evolución que 'Sky' avala con datos. Ante el Hull registró la mayor cantidad de toques de un jugador del Arsenal en el área rival en lo que va de Premier (13). Se convirtió, también, en el jugador de la Liga inglesa que más ocasiones de gol (3,57) genera por cada 90'. Ha elevado, además, su porcentaje de éxito en el regate (del 50 al 55%), en los pases (del 78 al 87%) y en los centros completados (del 14 al 33%). Pierde, también, menos balones: de 18,7 a 14,2 por cada 90'. Madueke, aun así, cree que hay facetas en las que puede seguir evolucionando: "Me siento bien. Todavía hay cosas que puedo mejorar, pero siento la confianza de mi entrenador y de mis compañeros. El entrenador lleva tiempo insistiendo en que tengo que anticiparme a las jugadas". Una cosa está clara: Arteta ha ganado un nuevo 'cañón' para la causa.

articles.title: Kalyan Chaubey back in AIFF electoral college after Karnataka nomination cleared
articles.summary: New Delhi: All India Football Federation (AIFF) president Kalyan Chaubey has found a place in the electoral college after the Electoral Officer approved
articles.body: New Delhi: All India Football Federation (AIFF) president Kalyan Chaubey has found a place in the electoral college after the Electoral Officer approved Karnataka State Football Association’s request to replace Hanif Mohammed due to ill health. The development clears a crucial hurdle for the incumbent president ahead of the December 20 elections.In the electoral college published on Wednesday, Chaubey was listed as Karnataka’s representative alongside NA Haris, the Karnataka FA president and AIFF's vice president.Chaubey's candidature to become president again had taken a hit after his name was withdrawn by the Daman and Diu Football Association. It had created question marks over his participation in the election process.The KSFA had sought approval to alter its representation after the electoral college was initially finalised. The request was accepted by Electoral Officer Rajeev Sharma, who allowed the association to replace Hanif Mohammed with Chaubey.The change followed Hanif's written request to withdraw from the electoral college on medical grounds. The KSFA subsequently sought the substitution, with the Electoral Officer accepting the request after examining the circumstances and the applicable provisions governing changes to delegates.The Karnataka association's request had raised questions over whether a change sought after the prescribed deadline would be permitted.The electoral officer's order cited provisions that allow a member association to nominate its representative, while also making clear that any alteration to the electoral college after the stipulated deadline requires approval. The request was ultimately allowed, with the withdrawal accepted and Chaubey's inclusion approved.The development also brings an interesting political dynamic into the AIFF election. Haris is a Congress politician, while Chaubey has political affiliations with the BJP. The two were part of the leadership that emerged after the 2022 elections, when Chaubey defeated former India captain Bhaichung Bhutia to become AIFF president.Chaubey's presidency has come under scrutiny in recent weeks. Former India internationals, including Bhaichung Bhutia, have sought the intervention of Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, raising concerns about the functioning of the federation and the direction of Indian football ahead of the election.With the electoral college now finalised and Chaubey's inclusion confirmed, attention shifts to the contest for the AIFF's top position. The federation's elections are scheduled to be held in New Delhi on December 20.How Karnataka State Football Association (KSFA) changed its nomination:November 15: The draft electoral college lists N.A. Haris and Hanif Mohammed as Karnataka State Football Association's representatives.November 15: Daman and Diu Football Association withdraws Kalyan Chaubey's nomination as an AIFF election voter, retaining Walter Pereira and Altamash Shaikh as its delegates.November 16: Hanif Mohammed writes to the KSFA Honorary General Secretary, seeking withdrawal of his name from the AIFF electoral college on medical grounds, citing physical and mental stress as well as long-distance travel.November 18 (1:58 pm): KSFA president NA Haris forwards an official request to the Electoral Officer, seeking approval under Article 4.2 of Schedule III to nominate himself and Kalyan Chaubey as the association's representatives.November 18 (4:27 pm): The Electoral Officer's office asks KSFA to submit a medical certificate supporting Hanif's withdrawal.November 19: KSFA submits a medical certificate dated November 14 from Dr Pankaj Singhai, Consultant Physician, Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru. The certificate advises Hanif to avoid long-distance travel and stress and to take rest.November 24: The Electoral Officer approves KSFA's request, accepts Hanif's withdrawal and permits Kalyan Chaubey to replace him as the association's representative, alongside N.A. Haris.November 25: The revised electoral college is published, listing N.A. Haris and Kalyan Chaubey as Karnataka's two representatives for the AIFF elections.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New leaked files expose Gianni Infantino’s $20B FIFA plan to lock away World Cup commercial rights for 96 years and offer tens of millions in executive bonuses
articles.summary: Leaked documents unveil FIFA's $20 billion plan to transfer World Cup commercial rights for 96 years and offer massive executive bonuses, sparking controversy and scrutiny of Infantino's leadership.
articles.body: FIFA's abandoned private equity proposal was considerably more far-reaching than a conventional investment deal. Documents exchanged with Thrive Capital, the firm founded by Joshua Kushner, reveal plans to transfer the commercial rights to FIFA events into a new $20 billion subsidiary for 96 years, while also allowing for potentially tens of millions of dollars in executive bonuses. The disclosures offer a closer look at a project that became one of the biggest controversies of Gianni Infantino's presidency.FIFA planned to transfer World Cup rights for 96 yearsLeaked documents reviewed by The Associated Press reveal that FIFA's proposed private equity arrangement would have given a new commercial subsidiary control of the organisation's event rights for almost a century.The plan, known internally as Project Box, involved creating FIFA Forward Enterprises (FFE), a for-profit subsidiary valued at approximately $20 billion. Under the proposed structure, the commercial rights to FIFA events would have been transferred to the company for exploitation over the following 96 years.A FIFA in-house risk assessment, included among the documents reviewed by the AP, described the arrangement in direct terms:“This deal provides for Fifa to create a for-profit subsidiary which would have all the commercial rights for FIFA events transferred to it for commercial exploitation for the next 96 years”.The assessment also revealed that FIFA's own finance officials had limited involvement in developing the transaction.“Were not directly privy to the construction of this transaction,” the document stated of the finance officials.The proposal had been moving towards completion in New York during the weekend of the men's World Cup final on July 19. However, the project only became public nine days after Spain defeated Argentina in the final, triggering a backlash that included criticism from senior figures within FIFA itself.The opposition intensified over concerns about the scale of the proposed transfer, the lack of transparency surrounding negotiations and the concentration of commercial control within a new company. Infantino subsequently withdrew the proposal within days.Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital emerged as anchor investorThe leaked papers also shed light on how FIFA selected its prospective investment partner and the negotiations that preceded the proposed agreement.FIFA had initially held discussions with Affinity Partners, the investment firm founded by Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump. It subsequently moved towards Thrive Capital, the firm led by Jared's younger brother, Joshua Kushner, as the proposed anchor investor.One of the documents explained why FIFA had not opened a formal tender process, citing “the specific and unique nature of the proposed investment, bilateral and unilateral conversations held with interest from several potential investment sources”.Affinity Partners was referenced in that explanation, indicating that the firm had been among the investment groups involved in discussions before Thrive emerged as the preferred partner.Thrive prepared a document titled Backstop Letter and Transaction Terms, dated July 17, setting out the proposed arrangement with FIFA under the Project Box name. The timing placed the negotiations close to the completion of the men's World Cup, with the new subsidiary potentially becoming a major vehicle for the organisation's commercial operations.The documents also included provisions for a management incentive plan, under which executives at FFE could receive bonuses worth tens of millions of dollars.Those payments would have been determined by the subsidiary's board, which was to be chaired by FIFA's sitting president, Infantino.FIFA defended the proposed structure in a statement, saying:“This is customary for proposed structures of this nature”.The organisation also stressed that the project remained a proposal and would have required approval from its 211 member federations, which effectively own FIFA as a Switzerland-based non-profit organisation.“FIFA's leadership would only have had leading roles in the board, which would not have led to any additional remuneration,” the governing body said.The distinction was significant because the documents outlined potential executive bonuses within the subsidiary, while FIFA maintained that its own leadership would not receive additional remuneration through their board positions.Infantino faces scrutiny over leadership and political tiesThe controversy surrounding Project Box has added to existing concerns about Infantino's leadership style and his relationship with the Trump administration.His ties to the US president have already attracted criticism, particularly over FIFA's decision to create a peace prize and its handling of disciplinary rules at the World Cup. One issue concerned the waiver of a mandatory one-match suspension for United States forward Folarin Balogun.The proposed private equity arrangement intensified concerns among senior figures in European football and officials in Japan, where questions have been raised about FIFA's governance and the extent to which major decisions are being developed within Infantino's inner circle.The leaked documents were first reported by the New York Post on Monday. Their disclosure also comes amid a wider dispute between FIFA and UEFA, which has been seeking access to records relating to the proposed commercial rights sell-off.UEFA recently secured a legal victory in Manhattan after a judge rejected FIFA's attempt to block the release of the documents. The European governing body had filed court papers in August as part of a broader effort to challenge Infantino's presidency, including the possibility of a criminal complaint against him personally in Switzerland over alleged financial mismanagement.Those allegations remain separate from the disclosures about Project Box, and the leaked papers do not by themselves establish wrongdoing.Infantino faces first presidential election challenge since 2016The latest disclosures arrive as Infantino prepares for his first contested presidential election since taking charge of FIFA in 2016.Two opponents are campaigning against him ahead of the March 18 vote in Morocco: Philippe Diallo of France and Kohzo Tashima of Japan. Infantino is nevertheless widely expected to secure another term.The election will take place against the backdrop of growing scrutiny over how FIFA conducts its commercial and governance affairs, with the abandoned private equity plan providing opponents and critics with a significant example of the concerns surrounding his administration.The proposed FFE structure would have placed FIFA's event-related commercial rights inside a separate for-profit company for 96 years, with a potential valuation of $20 billion and an executive incentive programme worth tens of millions of dollars. FIFA ultimately withdrew the proposal, but the documents now provide a more detailed account of how far the negotiations had progressed before the plan collapsed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Málaga comunica el adiós de Loren Juarros
articles.standfirst: El burgalés deja el cargo tras tres temporadas y media
articles.summary: El burgalés deja el cargo tras tres temporadas y media
articles.body: Loren Juarros pone punto final a su etapa como director deportivo del Málaga CF después de algo más de tres años en Martiricos. El burgalés llegó en 2023 con el complicado reto de devolver al club al fútbol profesional y se marcha con el equipo en Primera División, después de protagonizar dos ascensos que ya forman parte de la historia reciente de la entidad. El gol de Cordero en Tarragona y la irrupción de 'Los Bichos' representan los grandes hitos de su gestión. Sin embargo, su trayectoria también deja sombras, especialmente en la planificación de las últimas ventanas de mercado y el rendimiento de varios fichajes. La confección de la plantilla para el regreso a Primera ha terminado pesando demasiado, con un balance de cinco puntos de los últimos 39 posibles que ha precipitado su salida. Su primera gran decisión fue mantener a Sergio Pellicer en el banquillo, una apuesta que terminó dando sus frutos con el ascenso a Segunda. Para construir aquel equipo llegaron futbolistas como Alfonso Herrero, Dioni, Víctor García, Manu Molina, Nelson Monte o Galilea, mientras que la Academia aportó talento diferencial con Roberto Fernández, Larrubia, Kevin y Cordero. La temporada siguiente, el objetivo era consolidarse en el fútbol profesional. Pastor, Luismi y Lobete ofrecieron respuestas positivas, aunque operaciones como las de Baturina, Rahmani o Castel no alcanzaron las expectativas. La falta de un delantero en el mercado invernal obligó a buscar soluciones en casa, con la irrupción de Chupe, en una campaña que acabó con la permanencia y nuevas dudas sobre la continuidad de Pellicer. El proyecto dio otro giro en la temporada 2025/26. Pese a un mercado ambicioso, con nombres como Joaquín Muñoz, Dotor, Adrián Niño, Montero, Jauregi, Dorrio y Brasanac, el equipo fue perdiendo competitividad hasta caer a los puestos de descenso. La destitución de Pellicer abrió la puerta a Juanfran Funes, elegido después de que no fructificaran las alternativas de Kenan Kodro y Montanier. El técnico lojeño transformó al equipo y protagonizó una segunda vuelta extraordinaria que culminó con los ascensos frente a Las Palmas y Almería. Aquel éxito reforzó la posición de Loren, que amplió su contrato hasta 2028. Sin embargo, el salto a Primera exigía un nuevo nivel de exigencia y la planificación no estuvo a la altura: Calero, Juan Cruz, Dotor, Salinas, Pablo Martínez, Aznou, Berrocal y Cajuste no han conseguido dar el salto competitivo que necesitaba la plantilla. El balance de Loren Juarros deja una herencia de dos caras. Se marcha con el Málaga de vuelta a la élite y con el mérito de haber apostado por una generación de canteranos que ha devuelto la ilusión a La Rosaleda. También impulsó el trabajo de La Academia y el Acuerdo Marco con los clubes de la provincia. No obstante, quedan interrogantes sobre el rendimiento de las categorías inferiores y, sobre todo, sobre la capacidad de la dirección deportiva para construir una plantilla competitiva en Primera. Dos ascensos avalan su trayectoria, pero una última planificación deficiente ha terminado condicionando su despedida.

articles.title: Quote of the Day by Aristotle, "In life, first, have a definite, clear practical ideal; a goal, an objective. Second, have the necessary.."
articles.summary: Aristotle needs no introduction. His legacy is timeless.
articles.body: Aristotle needs no introduction. His legacy is timeless. Aristotle was one of the greatest philosophers, thinkers and intellectual figures in the history of humankind. Born in ancient Greece more than 2,300 years ago, he made outstanding contributions to philosophy, science, politics, ethics, biology, literature and education. His ideas helped to shape the development of Western civilisation and influenced generations of scholars, scientists, religious thinkers and political philosophers.He was so influential that his thoughts were central to intellectual discussions for centuries and many of the questions he asked are still debated today.Aristotle was born in 384 BC in Stagira, a town in northern Greece; thus he is sometimes called the Stagirite. His father, Nicomachus, was a physician in the service of King Amyntas III of Macedon. Aristotle’s father was a physician and this early exposure to medicine and natural observation may have contributed to his lifelong love of biology and the natural sciences. Orphaned at a young age, Aristotle was brought up by a guardian. With age his intellectual curiosity and his interest in learning became more and more evident.Around the age of 17 or 18 he went to Athens, one of the most important intellectual centers of the ancient Greek world, to study at Plato's Academy. Plato was one of the greatest philosophers of his time and had a great influence on him. He studied at the Academy for about 20 years, first as a student, then as a teacher and scholar. He had great respect for Plato , but eventually developed his own philosophical ideas which differed from those of his teacher .Plato was very concerned with the ideal forms that existed outside of the physical world, whereas Aristotle believed that knowledge could be obtained by studying the world around us. He believed that to understand reality one must use observation, evidence and logical reasoning. This difference of approach would become one of the great distinctions in the history of philosophy.His relationship with Alexander the GreatIn 343 BC , Aristotle was invited by King Philip II of Macedon to tutor his son , Alexander , who would later be known as Alexander the Great - this was one of the most interesting chapters in Aristotle's life. The young prince was tutored by Aristotle in subjects such as philosophy, literature, politics, medicine and ethics. He also introduced him to Greek culture and to the works of important literary figures, especially Homer.The exact nature of the relationship and the extent of Aristotle’s influence on Alexander is a matter of historical debate, but this connection brought together two of the most extraordinary figures of the ancient world: one who would come to change the political world through his military conquests, and one who would change the intellectual world through his philosophical and academic contributions. At last Aristotle returned to Athens after Alexander had begun his wars.The foundation of the LyceumIn 335 BC, Aristotle opened his own school in Athens, named the Lyceum. It was an important center of philosophical discussion, scientific research and intellectual education. Unlike many traditional teaching institutions, Aristotle’s school provided students with the opportunity to explore different subjects by means of observation, discussion, research and systematic reasoning.His students were known as Peripatetics, a term that has been associated with the practice of walking about while conversing on philosophical matters. Aristotle and his students studied an impressive range of subjects at the Lyceum including mathematics, astronomy, politics, zoology, botany, literature and metaphysics. Aristotle believed education should aid in developing the ability to think critically and understand the world, not just memorise information. His methods provided the foundation for systematic academic inquiry.His major philosophical contributionsAristotle’s philosophical contributions were remarkable because he tried to understand nearly every aspect of human life.One of his most important works was the Nicomachean Ethics, where he talked about the meaning of happiness and the virtues necessary for a good life. He thought that the ultimate purpose of human life was to achieve eudaimonia, a Greek word that is often translated as flourishing or living well. He argued that true happiness did not come from wealth, pleasure or social recognition alone. Instead it came from having good character and practising virtues such as courage, honesty, generosity, patience and wisdom.He also suggested the idea of the Golden Mean, that virtue is often found between two extremes. Thus courage is a mean between cowardice and rashness; generosity between meanness and prodigality. His philosophy encouraged people to cultivate balance, to exercise good judgement and to develop habits that would help them become better human beings.Aristotle was among the first to study logic. He developed a logical system for reasoning , and examined the methods by which conclusions might be drawn from stated premises .His work on syllogisms provided an important foundation for the development of formal logic. He believed that knowledge could be obtained only through clear thinking and sound reasoning.Aristotle's "Politics" is a study of the nature of government, citizenship, and the responsibilities of individuals in society. He thought that human beings were inherently social and political animals, capable of fulfilling their potential in communal life. He studied different types of governments . He looked at the good and bad of these governments . He also thought the goal of a political community was to foster the common good and to set the terms under which citizens could have fulfilling lives.Aristotle also made a lasting contribution to literary criticism in his Poetics . Here he studied tragedy, story telling, character development and the emotional effect of dramatic literature. Especially influential was his discussion of catharsis, normally taken to mean the emotional release or clarification that audiences experience in tragedy. His ideas still inform discussions of storytelling, theatre, cinema and literary criticism.LegacyAristotle was more than a philosopher musing about the world. He was also an observant naturalist. He studied animals, noted their physical characteristics, classified different species, and tried to understand their behaviour and reproductive processes. His biological writings are particularly remarkable for their scope and observation. Some of his scientific findings were later corrected, but his systematic method of studying living things had an effect on natural history for centuries. He also worked in physics, astronomy and metaphysics. Many of his scientific explanations were later replaced by modern discoveries, but his insistence on probing basic questions helped form the intellectual traditions that followed.Anti-Macedonian feeling arose in Athens after the death of Alexander the Great in 323 BC. Aristotle was associated with the Macedonian royal family and was politically unpopular, and even accused of impiety. He left Athens and moved to Chalcis where he spent his last days. Aristotle died in 322 BC, at the age of about 62. He left behind a remarkable intellectual heritage, much of it surviving and becoming foundational to the development of philosophy and scholarship.Quote of the Day"In life first, have a definite, clear practical ideal; a goal, an objective. Second, have the necessary means to achieve your ends; wisdom, money, materials, and methods. Third, adjust all your means to that end." It is a deep, meaningful quote which is widely attributed to Aristotle.These lines teach us a profound lesson on the relationship between ambition, preparation and purposeful action. This quote reminds us that success is seldom accidental. You can’t just dream about doing something or hope for a better life. We need to know what we want, understand what it will take to get there and consciously organise our resources and efforts toward making that ambition a reality.. It means that meaningful achievements start with a clear purpose and are achieved through smart use of available resources.The first part of the quote is: “First, have a definite, clear practical ideal; a goal, an objective. This is probably the most fundamental rule of getting anything meaningful in life. Before we start our trip, we need to know where we are going. The greatest effort, even the most sincere effort, can go around in circles without a destination.Everyone has dreams and ambitions and aspirations but not everyone takes the time to clarify them. Someone might say they want to be successful, financially independent or happy. But these are general desires, not specific aims. What does success look like for them? What does financial freedom look like? What would make them feel fulfilled?But it is necessary to distinguish between wanting and having a definite aim. A dream gives us something to hope for, a goal gives us something to work toward. Ambition needs clarity to provide direction. This helps us prioritise our decisions, avoid unnecessary distractions, and recognise whether our actions are taking us closer to our desired destination. The second part of the quote is as follows: “Second, have the means necessary to accomplish your ends; wisdom, money, materials, and methods. In this passage Aristotle draws attention to a fact which people tend to forget: the desire for a thing is not the willingness to get it. Ambition must be backed up by the right resources, knowledge and capabilities. A person may have a great idea, but without the required skills, financial resources, tools or practical knowledge, it can become difficult to turn that idea into reality. That's why preparation is as important as aspiration. Interestingly, Aristotle considers wisdom to be one of the essential means of achievement. This is important because having resources doesn’t guarantee success. Money can buy opportunities, but wisdom tells us how to use it. Work can be done with materials and tools, but knowledge allows us to use them effectively. Methods give us structure, experience helps us know what methods are likely to work.You use AI every day. articles.title: Raheem Sterling handed suspended prison sentence after crashing £270,000 Lamborghini while inhaling laughing gas from balloon while driving
articles.summary: Raheem Sterling has been handed a suspended prison sentence for dangerous driving after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini while inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon. The court also mandated community service and a two-year driving ban.
articles.body: Raheem Sterling has received a suspended prison sentence after admitting dangerous driving while inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon during a rush-hour journey that ended with his £270,000 Lamborghini crashing into a roadside barrier. The former England international told the court he had spent 12 days in rehabilitation for his use of the substance, which a judge said had become a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in his career.Sterling sentenced after dangerous driving and nitrous oxide offencesSterling, 31, was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on Wednesday after pleading guilty to dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation.He must also complete 100 hours of unpaid community service and has been disqualified from driving for two years. The court ordered him to pay a victim surcharge of £187 and prosecution costs of £85.In her sentencing remarks, District Judge Kirsty Allman revealed that Sterling had contacted UK Addiction Treatment on June 15 and subsequently entered rehabilitation for 12 days at Banbury Lodge.The judge said nitrous oxide had “become a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in his career”. She also referred to Sterling's position as a role model when explaining the sentence.His MBE, charitable work and time spent in rehabilitation were among the mitigating factors considered by the court. Although the sentence does not require him to undergo further therapeutic treatment, the lead therapist at Banbury Lodge believes additional support would be beneficial.Sterling showed little reaction as the sentence was delivered. He arrived wearing a black quarter-zip jumper, white T-shirt and black trousers, and sat in the glass dock with his back against the wall, maintaining eye contact with the judge as she read her remarks.The suspended sentence means he will not serve the 12 months in prison unless he breaches the conditions of the suspension or commits another offence that activates it.Four police reports before Lamborghini crashed into barrierThe offences took place on May 28, when Sterling drove his black Lamborghini Urus across several roads in Surrey and Hampshire while inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon.He pleaded guilty in September to dangerous driving on the M25, M3, A327 and Minley Road. He also admitted possessing six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen and driving dangerously while impaired.Prosecutor Simon Jones told an earlier hearing that police received a series of calls between 7.45am and 8.52am from motorists concerned about the way the Lamborghini was being driven.Witness Christopher Jennings called 999 at 7.49am after travelling alongside Sterling on the M25. Jones told the court that Jennings “was shocked by what he saw” and reported seeing the footballer inhaling from a balloon.Another witness, Fiona Jennings, was driving southbound on the M3 at approximately 8.45am when she noticed the vehicle repeatedly moving between lanes.She described the driving as “absolutely horrendous”, with the Lamborghini “swerving in and out of lanes”, the court heard.Jones told the hearing:“She had genuine concerns the driver might kill someone.”Fiona Jennings initially thought an airbag was involved when she looked across at the driver, but realised she was seeing a large inflated white balloon, with its neck in the driver's mouth.Dashcam footage released by the Crown Prosecution Service showed the Lamborghini switching lanes repeatedly before striking a concrete barrier on the right-hand side of the road and continuing its journey.After leaving the M3 at junction 4a, Sterling travelled along the A327 and completed a loop before losing control shortly after a roundabout. The vehicle left the carriageway and collided with either a road sign or metal gate, causing substantial damage. All four wheels were damaged, leaving the car unable to continue.Four police forces had received reports about the vehicle before the journey ended in the crash.Arrest, six canisters and admission of a nitrous oxide problemPolice body-worn camera footage showed Sterling inside the damaged Lamborghini when officers arrived at approximately 9.15am. Two canisters were visible on his lap as an officer told him: “You can put that down mate.”He was subsequently taken to Basingstoke police investigation centre. According to Jones, Sterling told custody staff that “he had a problem with nitrous oxide”.Sterling completed an impairment test but sought legal advice before deciding whether to provide a blood sample. The prosecutor said that, in the police sergeant's view, he was “deliberately failing to provide a clear answer”.During a later police interview, with legal representation present, Sterling accepted that he had been driving the vehicle but gave no-comment answers when questioned about his driving.At the September hearing, his barrister, Jason Bartfeld KC, accepted that the case fell into the “top category” of dangerous driving because of the prolonged journey and periods of serious impairment.However, the defence disputed the seriousness of the damage caused to the vehicle and argued that there had been “confusion” surrounding Sterling's failure to provide a specimen.The court ultimately considered his guilty pleas, rehabilitation and personal circumstances before imposing the suspended prison sentence.From four Premier League titles to an uncertain football futureSterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, becoming an important figure under Gareth Southgate. He helped the national team reach the semi-finals of the 2018 World Cup in Russia and the final of Euro 2020, where England lost to Italy on penalties.Born in Kingston, Jamaica, Sterling moved to England as a child and began his football development at Queens Park Rangers before joining Liverpool's academy. He made his senior debut at Anfield and established himself as one of the Premier League's most prominent young attackers.Manchester City signed him in 2015, and he went on to win four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019 during his time at the Etihad Stadium.He moved to Chelsea in 2022 but struggled to establish a regular place in the side and spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal. After leaving Stamford Bridge, he joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term agreement running until the end of the season. He is currently without a club.Sterling was appointed a Member of the Order of the British Empire in the 2021 Queen's Birthday Honours for services to racial equality in sport. He had become a prominent voice against racism and discrimination in football, speaking publicly about abuse directed at players and supporting campaigns promoting equality.His advocacy included speaking out amid controversy over England supporters booing players who took the knee before matches as a gesture against racism and intolerance.The court's decision brings the criminal proceedings over the May incident to sentencing, but Sterling now faces an 18-month suspended sentence, a two-year driving ban and 100 hours of unpaid work.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Así vivimos el Slavia de Praga 0-1 Villarreal

El contexto también presiona al conjunto local. El Slavia encadena 23 partidos sin ganar en la Champions League , igualando el récord negativo de la competición, mientras que el Villarreal tampoco atraviesa su mejor momento europeo tras haber ganado solo uno de sus últimos 15 encuentros en el torneo. Con dos jornadas antes del parón navideño, el encuentro adquiere un carácter decisivo para ambos, especialmente para el equipo de Iñigo Pérez, que necesita reaccionar después de encajar tres derrotas en las cuatro primeras jornadas.

articles.title: Eric Morris, Oklahoma State Reportedly Agree to New Contract amid Mestemaker's Breakout Season
articles.summary: In his first year as Oklahoma State head coach, Eric Morris is already being rewarded with a new deal.
articles.body:
In his first year as Oklahoma State head coach, Eric Morris is already being rewarded with a new deal.

According to ESPN's Pete Thamel , Morris and Oklahoma State have agreed to a new six-year deal that will extend his contract by two years through the 2032 season. The extension reportedly "includes a significant pay raise."

The Cowboys are 7-4 behind star quarterback Drew Mestemaker's breakout campaign.

After leading North Texas to an 11-2 record in 2025, Morris was hired to replace Mike Gundy at Oklahoma State, which had finished the year at 1-11. Mestemaker transferred from North Texas to join Morris with the Cowboys, and they continued to make magic together.

Morris made an immediate splash when he earned his first win at Oklahoma State against then-No. 6 Oregon in Week 2, which ended the Cowboys' 21-game losing streak against FBS opponents. The team has a 5-3 record in Big 12 play entering Saturday's regular-season finale against Kansas.

Mestemaker skyrocketed up NFL draft boards amid his stellar season. He leads FBS with 3,533 passing yards and ranks second with 30 touchdowns. ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr. recently named him the No. 1 quarterback prospect in the 2027 draft class. B/R's NFL Scouting Department predicted in its latest mock draft that he would be the first QB off the board, going at No. 3 to the Miami Dolphins.

Keeping Morris in the fold continues Oklahoma State's upward trajectory as it tries to reestablish itself as a national powerhouse. The Cowboys should feel confident in his ability to rebuild the program and attract top recruits following his development of Mestemaker.

articles.body: Brahim Díaz es noticia: el jugador madridista fue nominado como uno de los cinco candidatos a mejor jugador africano del año 2026, en un premio otorgado por la CAF (Confederación Africana de Fútbol). articles.title: El Madrid acaricia el Top-8 por primera vez
articles.standfirst: Los blancos no se han metido entre los mejores de la Fase Liga desde que se instauró el nuevo formato, en la 24-25
articles.summary: Los blancos no se han metido entre los mejores de la Fase Liga desde que se instauró el nuevo formato, en la 24-25
articles.body: Con cinco partidos disputados, el Real Madrid suma 15 puntos en la edición 26-27 de la Champions League. El registro no debería ser noticioso para el 15 veces campeón de Europa, pero sí lo es. Al menos, desde que la Copa de Europa instauró su nuevo formato, en la temporada 24-25. En aquel momento, el Madrid era el vigente campeón (conquistó el título en la final de Wembley ante el Dortmund), un hito del que ha estado lejos en las dos últimas temporadas. Con tres partidos por delante (Arsenal y Shakhtar, a domicilio, y LASK en el Bernabéu), en teoría apenas una victoria separa a los blancos del Top-8, el gran objetivo del club en esta primera fase de la Champions. José Mourinho lo verbalizó con claridad en la previa del partido ante el PSV. "Los 12 puntos nos dan la tranquilidad... pero hay que seguir que no queremos jugar el playoff", dijo Mou antes del duelo ante los holandeses, tras el que su equipo mantuvo el pleno europeo; cinco de cinco. El propio Mou sabe de lo que habla. La temporada pasado, él fue el entrenador rival del Madrid en el playff, una ronda de dieciseisavos de final a la que fue precisamente su equipo, el Benfica, el que condenó al Madrid. En el último partido de la Fase Liga, al Madrid le bastaba un empate para evitar esa ronda previa, pero un gol de portero de las Águilas, el ucraniano Trubin, en el tiempo de descuento, sacó al Madrid del grupo de cabeza y metió en el playoff al Benfica. Luego, el bombo tuvo el capricho de volver a emparejarlos, en un cruce marcado por los insultos racistas de Prestianni a Vinicius en el partido de ida, jugado en Lisboa. Fue una eliminatoria de desgaste extra para el Madrid, que para entonces ya estaba bajo el mando de Álvaro Arbeloa, tras el despido de Xabi Alonso en el mes de enero, después de la derrota en la final de la Supercopa de España ante el Barcelona. Aún con el vasco en el banquillo el Madrid acabó la Fase Liga con tres derrotas (Liverpool, City y Benfica, con Arbeloa recién aterrizado), lo que le condenó a jugar el playoff tras acabar la liguilla en novena posición. En la temporada anterior, todavía bajo el reinado de Carlo Ancelotti, al Madrid le fue incluso peor. De hecho, perdió tres de sus cinco primeros partidos europeos (Lille, Milan y Liverpool), y aunque ganó los tres últimos, sólo pudo ser undécimo. Además, en aquella ocasión el playoff le enfrentó a una de las grandes potencias del continente, aunque víctima habitual de los blancos en la historia reciente de la Champions. El City de Guardiola se inclinó ante el defensor del título, que ganó tanto en el Etihad como en el Bernabéu, antes del famoso cruce ante el Atlético que se decidió por el doble toque de Julián Alvarez en la tanda del Metropolitano. El Arsenal acabó en cuartos con la trayectoria europea de aquel Madrid, como el Bayern lo hizo la temporada pasada, aunque los blancos estuvieron mucho más cerca de las semifinales ante los alemanes que ante los ingleses. Ahora, con 15 puntos, el Madrid mira a todos los equipos del torneo, con la excepción del PSG, por el retrovisor. Una victoria más asegura de forma virtual el Top-8, y la posibilidad de aparcar la Champions hasta el mes de marzo. Sin duda, un balón de oxígeno y una baza extra en la pelea por la Liga, además del alivio de la presión que siempre supone un cruce extra en la Copa de Europa.

articles.title: Sociedad ucraniana para el Girona
articles.standfirst: Vanat y Pyshchur, que se complementan de maravilla, se hacen con un sitio en el once de Quique Álvarez
articles.summary: Vanat y Pyshchur, que se complementan de maravilla, se hacen con un sitio en el once de Quique Álvarez
articles.body: El Girona venció al Eibar 2-1 en la última jornada consiguiendo tres puntos de oro para situarse en la tercera posición de la tabla y mantenerse a una distancia límite con el ascenso directo, dos posiciones ocupadas por Almería y Castellón, a un ritmo y una proyección de puntos infernal, casi nunca visto. Los catalanes, que ya venían de remontar y sumar los tres puntos en el Carlos Tartiere contra el Oviedo (1-2), volvieron a aprovechar el buen momento -y sorprendente para muchos- del ucraniano Pyshchur. El gigantón fue el gran protagonista en tierras asturianas y confirmó su línea ascendente de rendimiento para seguir en el once del equipo, ante el Eibar, al lado de su compatriota Vanat, una vez retornado este de la convocatoria con su selección. Los dos atacantes del este se complementaron de maravilla y se movieron por diferentes zonas para generar confusión en la defensa guipuzcoana, puntos de remate distintos y líneas de asociación con sus compañeros. De hecho, Vanat marcó su sexto gol en el campeonato aprovechando una asistencia de Pyshchur, que más adelante estrelló un remate tras un saque de esquina a la base del palo de la portería de Magunagoitia. La sociedad que forman los futbolistas ha obligado a Quique Álvarez a usar un 4-4-2 dejando a un lado su preferido 4-2-3-1 o 4-3-3. Y es que, el propio técnico, analizando el partido ante el Eibar admitió que echa en falta una pieza más por dentro como nexo de unión. articles.title: John Motson to Be Added to EA Sports FC 27 in 'Digital Tribute' to Legendary Commentator
articles.summary: The iconic voice of commentator John Motson will return to EA Sports FC with a "digital tribute" built on old recordings and artificial intelligence.
articles.body:
The iconic voice of commentator John Motson will return to EA Sports FC with a "digital tribute" built on old recordings and artificial intelligence.

Motson, who died in 2023, will feature in EA Sports FC 27 after the publisher worked with his family to recreate his likeness.

"We're honoured to bring back the iconic voice of John Motson, the legendary English football commentator and unmistakable voice of a decade of EA Sports football titles from 1996-2006," wrote EA Sports in a statement.

"With the blessing and partnership of Motson's family, EA Sports FC have worked with extensive care and respect to create a digital tribute to one of the game's greatest voices, inspiring a whole new generation of football fans."

The message also confirms EA built on "almost ten years of in-game recordings" to bring Motson back, utilizing "new AI-tools, bringing a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself."

Motson's tone will be familiar to anyone who grew up watching football on the BBC, where he worked for nearly half a century. He was also famous for his sheepskin coat, which is now included in the National Football Museum as an item of significant importance to English football history.

Although the use of generative AI in video games is a particularly controversial point for many, Motson's family are excited to hear his unmistakable voice back in the biggest football series in the world.

"My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA Sports FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game," said Fred Motson.

"His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole new set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary."

articles.summary: Y lo era. Final. La pega Grimaldo y el balón se va a la barrera. El rechace la pega Mendoza y el balón acaba en las manos de Beko. Puede que haya sido
articles.body:
Última hora del Atlético - Viking en directo:

¡Muy buenas tardes! ¡Bienvenidos a la Champions League! ¡Bienvenidos al Atlético-Viking! En poco más de dos horas, arranca en el Metropolitano uno de los duelos de esta quinta jornada de la liguilla de la máxima competición, un choque que se antoja clave para los de Simeone.

Los rojiblancos no pueden permitirse más tropiezos que compliquen la posición que se han ganado en el continente desde que Simeone se hiciera cargo del banquillo conquistando la Copa, primero, y convirtiera a su equipo en un fijo de las rondas de eliminación de la Champions, en las temporadas sucesivas.

Ambos equipos llegan al duelo de esta noche empatados a cuatro puntos pero con diferentes estados de ánimo. El Atlético necesita ganar para seguir aspirando al Top 8 mientras que los noruegos están viviendo un sueño jugando la Champions.

La gran novedad en la convocatoria de Simeone es el regreso de Marc Pubill. El lateral rojiblanco, con un esguince leve de tobillo desde el encuentro de la Liga de Naciones entre España e Inglaterra, se perdió el último partido ante el Getafe, pero ya está listo para el choque de hoy en el Metropolitano.

Aún siguen de baja tanto Cuti Romero, por una dolencia muscular que lo ha impedido jugar cada uno de los últimos siete partidos del Atlético, como Ademola Lookman, con un esguince de rodilla de alto grado que lo mantendrá aún fuera en torno a un mes.

Con estos ingredientes, el Atlético está obligado a sacar adelante un partido en el que ya no tiene margen de error. Una vez hechas las presentaciones, ¡arrancamos!

articles.title: La clave del éxito de Bellingham: "Ha reducido sus salidas nocturnas"
articles.standfirst: La estrella del Madrid cambia sus hábitos tras una temporada en la que estuvo en el punto de mira
articles.summary: La estrella del Madrid cambia sus hábitos tras una temporada en la que estuvo en el punto de mira
articles.body: Jude Bellingham ha cambiado algunos de sus hábitos fuera del terreno de juego. Así lo aseguró Chitu en el programa 'Otra Ronda', donde abordó el debate sobre la vida extradeportiva del futbolista inglés y las informaciones relacionadas con sus salidas nocturnas. "Ha reducido el tema de salir, eso es verdad", afirmó. El centrocampista del Real Madrid ha estado en el foco de las críticas durante las últimas temporadas, al igual que otros compañeros de vestuario. En el programa se apuntó a que los futbolistas han pasado a estar en el centro de las críticas después de dos cursos en los que el equipo no ha estado a la altura de las expectativas. "Los jugadores, incluido Bellingham, se han visto en una situación en la que después de dos temporadas se les estaba señalando a ellos. Ya no era una cuestión de entrenadores", se explicó durante la conversación. Además, se destacó que la directiva también ha reaccionado en el mercado con varios fichajes, lo que habría cambiado el foco de las críticas. Otro de los aspectos que se abordaron fue la influencia de los entornos en las informaciones sobre la vida extradeportiva de los futbolistas. Chitu puso el acento en cómo pueden influir las opiniones procedentes del entorno del entrenador o incluso de compañeros que compiten por un puesto en el equipo. "Este tema concreto de la vida extradeportiva influye mucho por los entornos de cada uno, quién te cuenta cosas, el entorno del entrenador que no está contento con la actitud del jugador, incluso el entorno del futbolista que pelea por la titularidad", comentaron. Sin embargo, la reflexión más llamativa llegó al hablar de las posibles salidas nocturnas del inglés. Los tertulianos defendieron que lo verdaderamente importante es la respuesta del jugador cuando llega el momento de competir. “A mí, de verdad, si Jude Bellingham sale todas las noches y luego llega y hace lo que ha hecho hoy, que salga todas las noches, que no hay ningún problema”, destacaron. Una postura que dio pie a una referencia a la estrategia de Romario, antes de insistir en que los hábitos personales de un futbolista no deberían convertirse en un problema si después responde sobre el césped. De esta manera, Bellingham habría reducido sus salidas nocturnas, aunque en 'Otra Ronda' también se defendió que el rendimiento deportivo debe estar por encima del ruido generado alrededor de su vida privada.

articles.title: El Villarreal no gana para sustos, pero se engancha a la Champions con fuerza
articles.standfirst: El submarino sufre la presión del Slavia en un partido en el que el VAR corrigió una roja a Veiga y un penalti de Gueye, tras un gol local que no valió por fuera de juego
articles.summary: El submarino sufre la presión del Slavia en un partido en el que el VAR corrigió una roja a Veiga y un penalti de Gueye, tras un gol local que no valió por fuera de juego
articles.body: El Villarreal se enganchó con las dos manos a la Champions tras sufrir ante el Slavia de Praga en un partido en el que no ganó para sustos hasta el final. El árbitro anuló un gol local por fuera de juego. Y después, el VAR rectificó, bien, una roja a Veiga y un penalti de Gueye en la segunda parte. Al final valió el tanto de Buchanan para poner fin a siete derrotas seguidas a domicilio en Champions del submarino y dejar su portería a cero 15 encuentros después. No tardó ni diez segundos el Slavia de Praga en enseñar el colmillo. El saque de centro cayó al portero, patadón arriba y Suleiman se giró para bajar el balón y disparar con la izquierda. Luiz Júnior, a córner. Era el preludio de lo que le esperaba al submarino si no se quitaba el pijama ante un rival que agita el juego y presiona en todo el campo si es necesario. Si el plan era aguantar para que se cansaran, funcionaba a medias, porque el equipo checo manejaba el partido y no permitía que el Villarreal le hiciera daño. No había noticias de Gueye ni Maciá porque Novak y Sadílek no les permitían maniobrar. Con Moleiro bien tapado, al equipo de Iñigo le quedaba recurrir a lo que ya funcionaba: el contragolpe por las bandas. Un escorzo de Ayoze para puntear un balón que Oluwaseyi encontrara un pasillo, pero chutó a las manos de Markovic. Después fue Buchanan el que metió un buen centro tras galopar por el costado contrario, pero el balón se le quedó atrás a Tani. La primera mitad acabó con los reseñados repullos para los amarillos: gol anulado a Suleiman por fuera de juego y cambio de tarjeta roja por amarilla a Renato Veiga en una acción temeraria siendo el último jugador. Cabía esperar que el Slavia aflojara las tuercas en la segunda parte. Pero no. Jurasek continuaba llevando balones al área y logró conectar con Chytil, al que tapó en el último segundo Veiga. El submarino tenía que encontrar una grieta en el plan de los checos. Avisó Mouriño con una chilena muy bien dirigida a la que le faltó fuerza. Pero después fue Maciá el que robó un balón en el centro del campo para meter un pase a Ayoze. El delantero tinerfeño controló en el área y asistió para que Buchanan batiera a Markovic. La entrada de Kacor sirvió para que el Slavia cargara el juego por la izquierda que cerca estuvo de encontrar premio con un centro que no pudieron cerrar Veiga ni Costa. Iñigo entendió que había que proteger esa renta como fuera y cambió el dibujo a cinco defensas, aunque con la amenaza de Mikautadze arriba, que pudo sentenciar y no acertó. Otra vez el árbitro dejó sin aliento a los amarillos cuando pitó penalti de Gueye antes de un saque de esquina. Se repitió el córner, a instancias del VAR, ya sin consecuencias.

articles.title: El Málaga garantiza a Funes su continuidad en el banquillo
articles.standfirst: El entrenador tendrá oportunidad de convencer a Corona
articles.summary: El entrenador tendrá oportunidad de convencer a Corona
articles.body: La salida de Loren Juarros ha provocado movimientos inmediatos en la estructura del Málaga CF. Tras anunciarse el cese del director deportivo, la cúpula del club ha mantenido una reunión con Juanfran Funes para trasladarle un mensaje de confianza. El técnico granadino, que llegó al primer equipo hace poco más de un año procedente del filial, seguirá al frente del proyecto. La apuesta por el lojeño dio sus frutos durante la pasada temporada. Primero consiguió cambiar la dinámica de resultados y después encontró una versión futbolística que permitió a 'Los Bichos' alcanzar su mejor nivel. El desenlace fue el ascenso a Primera División, un objetivo que parecía complicado cuando asumió el banquillo. El escenario actual, sin embargo, es muy diferente. El Málaga atraviesa un inicio de temporada especialmente delicado, con apenas cinco puntos de los primeros 39 posibles y trece jornadas sin conocer la victoria. Una situación que ya ha provocado la salida de Loren Juarros, pero que, por ahora, no se llevará por delante al entrenador. La entidad considera que Funes tiene capacidad para cambiar el rumbo del equipo y confía en que pueda conducirlo hacia la permanencia, independientemente de quién termine ocupando la dirección deportiva, con Miguel Ángel Corona como uno de los principales candidatos. El mensaje trasladado al técnico ha sido claro: el club cuenta con él al cien por cien y no contempla, de momento, un cambio en el banquillo. Además, desde Martiricos quieren dejar atrás los últimos días de incertidumbre institucional y centrar todos los esfuerzos en el próximo compromiso liguero. El Athletic Club aparece como la primera oportunidad para romper la mala dinámica y conseguir esa victoria que todavía se resiste en LaLiga. La marcha de Loren Juarros también supone un cambio importante en el entorno de Funes. El entrenador siempre ha reconocido la estrecha relación profesional que mantenía con el burgalés, al que llegó a definir como parte de un «matrimonio deportivo». Ambos compartían una misma hoja de ruta, con especial atención al crecimiento de los futbolistas de La Academia y a la apuesta por el talento de la cantera. Funes pierde así a uno de sus principales respaldos dentro de la estructura deportiva. Ahora tendrá que afrontar el desafío de sacar al Málaga de la zona complicada sin Loren a su lado y con la obligación de encontrar respuestas sobre el terreno de juego.

articles.title: What Glenn Schumann said after being named FSU's coach
articles.summary: New Florida State Seminoles head coach Glenn Schumann thanks Kirby Smart and Nick Saban
articles.body:
The Georgia Bulldogs ware looking for a new defensive coordinator after the Florida State Seminoles named Glenn Schumann as their head coach. FSU signed Schumann to a five-year contract, but Schumann will be serving as Georgia 's defensive coordinator for the remainder of the college football season as UGA looks to make a run in the College Football Playoff.

Schumann, 36, is an excellent recruiter and has served under coach Kirby Smart during the entire Smart era at Georgia. The two were previously together at Alabama before coming to Athens.

Schumann will have a major challenge at Florida State . The Seminoles have struggled defensively and along the offensive line for much of the past decade-plus. Florida State has a rich history, but has not lived up to the high standards set during the Bobby Bowden and Jimbo Fisher eras.

"Being named the head coach at Florida State is an incredible honor and responsibility," Schumann said after Florida State hired him. The Seminoles have not made the playoff since the 2014 season. "I am thankful to President McCullough, Peter Collins, Jeff Purinton and the rest of the university's leadership for their belief in me. We are going to build a program that meets the championship expectation at Florida State through hard work, high standards and a commitment to each other.

"I want to thank Coach Smart and Coach Saban for their trust in me and supporting me with opportunities to develop as a coach and leader. I will be forever grateful for the impact they have had on my life. My family's connection to Florida State is deep, and I know what this program can be. I'm excited to bring my wife and children to a place that means so much to my family."

Schumann will be working double duty as he works to chase a national championship with Georgia while also trying to secure a quality signing class with Florida State. The early signing period is Dec. 2-4 while the transfer portal will be open Jan. 4-13 (with teams in the playoff having a five-day period after their final game to enter the portal).

articles.title: Manchester City: Football regulator chief 'has stomach' to take action against club
articles.summary: The chair of English football's independent regulator tells MPs he "has the stomach" to take potential action against Manchester City.
articles.body:
The chair of English football's independent regulator has told MPs he "has the stomach" to take potential action against Manchester City .

The club was found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-season period by an independent commission.

The verdict, published in September, found City's Abu Dhabi owners - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president Sheikh Mansour - inflated revenues and disguised losses by £900 million through "sham" arrangements.

City deny wronging and have appealed, but if the ruling is upheld, they could face an investigation by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR).

It has the power to remove directors if they are deemed unsuitable, and even to force a sale of the club.

Appearing in front of parliament's Digital, Culture, Media and Sport select committee, IFR chairman David Kogan was clear that the watchdog would not be afraid to investigate the club's hierarchy and take action, if deemed necessary.

"Forget the name of the club, forget the size of the club, forget the scale of the issue. We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size," he said.

"We absolutely will have to take the appropriate action as laid out in the legislation, depending on the circumstances as they come to us, which are the evidence that's been presented and collated by the independent commission of the Premier League and by any judgement that takes place on that evidence through an appeal.

"But in one sense, the evidence has already been judged by those cases having been found guilty, so we will absolutely have the stomach to do so.

"Would I, with an organisation that has a relatively new, fairly young staff, that's been going for less than a year, would I have chosen to have this particular issue in our laps this early? Well, probably not.

"But the truth is, if we don't act - assuming those circumstances are triggered - if we don't act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator?

"So I think we have to absolutely, clearly be seen to be doing the job that you as legislators have asked us to do, and we absolutely will do that, whatever that means."

De Bruyne's feelings for Man City will 'never change'

Premier League clubs to cover legal costs if Man City sponsors sue

The fallout from the case has prompted concern that wider UAE investment in UK projects could suffer. In September, Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for saying he would be "really concerned" if the scandal led to City's owners selling the club.

Kogan added: "Does the evidence, if we come to assess it in relation to individuals, stand up in terms of the legislation as being a cause for concern? And if it is, we will have to act appropriately.

"That is the only test, not the politics around it, not the place where it came from, not the size of the club. It is the only test because without that, you cannot have an effective regulator."

When asked how any possible legal battles with City would be paid for, IFR chief executive Richard Monks said a litigation reserve of £2m was to be built up over the next two years via a levy charged to the clubs. "When we take litigation, we expect to win and we expect to reclaim costs and repay that reserve from costs," he said.

"Now clearly - and I'm not talking about a specific case - clearly, there could be a very large legal case of any particular club that would require us to spend more than £2m in terms of litigation costs and barrister costs in particular. So if that happens, we have agreed with government [that it] will effectively lend us the money in terms of cash flow.

"As I say, we'd expect to win that litigation, to claim costs and repay government. If we failed in that massive litigation, then ultimately it would be added to the levy and we'd repay government that way."
