articles.title: 📸 Bruno & Man Utd strike it lucky in critical UCL clash vs Sporting
articles.summary: Bruno Fernandes may have breathed life into the early days of the Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United, and with a little help from the groundskeeper...
articles.body:
Bruno Fernandes may have breathed life into the early days of the Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United, and with a little help from the groundskeeper, too.

It was a calamitous first half from the Red Devils on the road in Lisbon against Sporting, with the in-form Luis Suárez making it one-nil from the spot in the 33rd minute, with United lucky to head into the half-time team talk down by just a single goal.

But it would not be a UCL night without further drama, and the home support at Estádio José Alvalade may ultimately leave the ground stunned come full-time after United have flipped the match on its head.

Fernandes, so often the talismanic figure at the heart of everything good going forward, levelled the scoreline just three minutes after the break from a converted penalty of his own.

It was the first goal of the Poch era, but Bruno was not done there, and just two minutes later, the Portuguese maestro would put United out in front and complete his brace on the night against his former club in unreal fashion.

Thanks to a massive deflection that saw his tame effort ultimately beat Brazilian shot-stopper Kaique Pereira, giving him four goals and one assist in five Champions League appearances this term.

With the potential reversal ~20 minutes away, can United's luck hold out in the wake of a horrendous weekend debut under their latest manager?

articles.title: Fiorentina’s Mastantuono problem isn’t just about Mastantuono
articles.summary: The Real Madrid loanee hasn’t helped the Viola much for reasons that have little to do with him as a player.
articles.body:
As I wrote yesterday about Radu Drǎgușin , Fiorentina has a lot of problems and focusing in on a single one risks missing the bigger picture. However, I'd argue that, over the course of the season, the biggest problem has been Franco Mastantuono. The young Argentine has shown tantalizing glimpses of the player he could become but hasn't contributed to winning for a team that desperately needs winning contributions.

I want to make it very clear that it's weird to criticize a 19-year-old, even one as precocious as Mastantuono. International superstardom is a tough row to hoe and I can't imagine the weight of expectations are easily borne by any shoulders, much less a teenager's. It's worth remembering that he's in his first season as a full-time starter in Europe, in a new country, learning a new language. For the first time in his career, he isn't employed by a juggernaut but by a club that, despite its ambitions, is mid-table fodder. His head is probably spinning and he deserves credit for what he's done well.

I want to list some of the things he's done well, too, because this article is going to focus on the other stuff. Mastantuono wants to work. He covers a lot of ground and plays with some fire in his belly. Unlike many luxury players, he isn't afraid to stick his foot in. He gets booted up in the air every game and never complains; he tries to play through contact instead of going to ground every time someone breathes on him. That fits in with his on-pitch character: he wants to be the best player. He wants all the responsibility of on-ball creativity and the spotlight that comes with it. He never hides. He never drifts out of games. He's obviously got a tremendous reservoir of self-belief, a mental strength that will stand him in good stead throughout his career.

For each of those positives qualities, though, there's a negative corr0lary. For all his running around, Mastantuono doesn't really help the team. He loves charging forward to close down a defender when the rest of the team has dropped into a deep block, which deforms the shape and forces everyone to rotate around much earlier than they ought to. It's the same with his tackles: he'll challenge for the ball but he's very bad at it, usually lunging as an opponent goes by. That also puts him out of position and forces his teammates to cover him, leaving their own assignments and yeah, you know what happens next. The whole shape collapses.

Mastantuono is supposed to be an individualist, of course. Real Madrid didn't send him to Florence to learn how to be a cog in a mid-table machine; it sent him to Florence to get as many on-ball reps as he could. By pushing the boundaries of what he's able to do, he'll expand his game, even if the immediate results are often frustrating. Superstars aren't supposed to worry about consequences. That's for the water carriers. The peons. Everyone else.

In Mastantuono's case, though, I think this course is a mistake for two reasons. First, he's not that kind of player. While he's quick and slippery, he lacks the elite physical gifts to blow by defenders. He's a good dribbler but not good enough to wriggle away from multiple markers. He's clever but lacks the galaxy-brained creativity to outfox a set defense. Maybe he'll develop one of those qualities but it looks more like he's banging his head into the flimsy cement of the Franchi over and over. You can push the boundaries of your ability but only so far. There's a maximum extent beyond which you cannot cross no matter how much you want to and how much you work.

That leads me to the second reason I think he's doing himself a disservice. If Mastantuono sees his future at Real Madrid, it probably won't be as a Kylian Mbappe or a Cristiano Ronaldo or one of the other all-time greats the club builds around. No, I think Mastantuono's best chance to stick is as a more functional player. Madrid always needs one attacker who does the dirty work of tracking back and running off ball and making simple passes to his more illustrious teammates. It's the only way to balance the team. Because Mastantuono's got a good engine, his best chance to stick at the Bernabeu is to embrace the dirty work. Instead, he's doing the exact opposite in Florence.

It's a tough situation for the kid. I think he's doing exactly as he was instructed by Jose Mourinho and the Real Madrid brass. The egocentric style of play doesn't necessarily reflect him as a player. It reflects him doing what his coaches told him to do this year at some anonymous Italian team that's lucky to bask in the reflected glory of his brilliance. If that doesn't help his team, well, he'll be gone in a few months. Just endure some discomfort, then come back home and see if you're ready to play for a real team.

And there's the root of the problem. Mastantuono's purpose this season isn't aligned with Fiorentina's. His job is to get better as a player regardless of impact on the team. If his improvement helps the team, that's an incidental bonus. The Viola, on the other hand, need consistent excellence from Mastantuono because they're contractually obligated to start him in as many games as possible. They need him to maybe not prostrate himself at the altar of team success but at least bow.

It's a situation that probably hasn't helped the team spirit. Here's this kid, this famous kid who's accomplished not much in his brief career, guaranteed a starting job regardless of performance. While he seems respectful enough, at the end of the day he's not accountable to Paolo Vanoli or to his current teammates; he's accountable to Real Madrid. That preferential treatment can destroy a team's morale and thus its effectiveness. Last year's swoon was partly motivated by Moise Kean's unique ability to avoid reprimand for things his colleagues would've been pulled up for. Mastantuono has done less than Kean in Serie A. The algebra is as simple as it is inevitable.

A dry loan for a budding talent doesn't scupper other clubs, of course, and there have been plenty of similar cases that were mutually beneficial. For both player and club to succeed in these circumstances requires a unity of organizational purpose, a long-term vision for the club, and expertise in combining them. It's not Mastantuono's fault that Fiorentina hasn't shown competence in any of those areas in years. For all the money spent this summer, there's one thing that the Viola can't buy: leadership. And until they find another way to acquire it, situations like Mastantuono's will be regular symptoms of an underlying condition.

articles.title: How UTSA's recharged culture fuels championship contention beyond the stats
articles.summary: The Roadrunners are hardly a statistical juggernaut, but they find ways to win, setting up an unlikely path to an American Conference championship.
articles.body:
At some point during team meetings each week, UTSA coach Jeff Traylor stands in front of the Roadrunners and sorts through some updated stats and rankings. More often than not, the numbers aren't very flattering.

No. 89 in the FBS in passing. No. 35 in rushing. No. 97 in total defense.

Traylor is far from surprised. After UTSA pulled out a 19-17 win against UAB last week, Traylor said he didn't believe the Roadrunners boast any unit that stands as the best in the American Conference between offense, defense and special teams.

But for all the holes in their resume and statistical profile, the Roadrunners are No. 1 in the place that matters most - the league standings. UTSA hosts Tulsa at 11 a.m. Friday in the Alamodome with a chance to secure home field in the American Conference championship game, riding an unorthodox formula built on attitude and intangibles to push toward one of the program's best seasons.

"How are you winning? Well, you sure as heck know it's not coaching, right?" Traylor said. "It's got to be those players, and it's Ubuntu, 'I am because we are.' We have the best culture in the country."

The Roadrunners have stressed that "Ubuntu" mindset since the start of the season, leaning on the African philosophy stating that an individual's success and well-being is tied to the success and well-being of those around them.

What else could explain how well the Roadrunners cover for each other despite rarely performing at a high level in all three facets? The defense carried UTSA to a 16-14 win against Rice, a 35-16 drubbing of North Texas and Saturday's 19-17 survival against UAB, while the offense was the biggest driver in two shootout wins: 59-45 against Colorado State and 38-34 against Navy.

"That's why this is the greatest team sport, because it's not who has the greatest special teams, or the greatest offense or defense," offensive lineman Ben Rios said. "It's really just who collectively has the best unit, and that's what I like about this team."

For Traylor, the identity is another sign that his retooled approach to roster construction is paying dividends. The Roadrunners "just recruited a different kind of kid" this cycle, Traylor said, prioritizing championship experience and character over talent and athleticism.

With the new team solidified and mostly on campus by January, the Roadrunners jumped into their identity and culture talks immediately rather than waiting until the start of preseason camp. UTSA's "Triangle of Toughness" has been a major talking point for Traylor dating to his first season in 2020, and he wanted to be sure this year's Roadrunners understood that before kickoff rather than learning through the season.

"Our culture, and our togetherness, and the Triangle of Toughness, is just, it's back to what it used to be," Traylor said.

A longtime high school coach, Traylor had grown used to instilling that culture over a four-year cycle with each player, allowing the veterans to set the tone for the newcomers.

He admits he "didn't do a very good job" of adjusting as that timeline tightened the previous two years. With transfer portal windows open in both the winter and following spring practice, Traylor's roster wasn't solidified until the summer, leaving less time for culture building.

Though college football is still transient by nature, Traylor took advantage of the move this year to eliminate the spring transfer window. By the end of January, the Roadrunners had built the roster they'd ride with through the year, leaving more time for an identity to take hold.

"Night and day. You could just tell from the locker room talk, and just the culture, and the guys in general," Rios said. "I know each and every person in my position room. I know their background, and that's just something that we've had in the past, but I just think that it's another level this year."

As UTSA's seniors prepare for their final regular-season home game Friday against Tulsa, Traylor stressed that the veteran returners were also critical to the recharged identity. He highlighted defensive lineman Tai Leonard for embodying that mindset, as the fifth-year senior turned down a single-digit jersey and pushed focus away from individual stats to instead concentrate on his role as a thankless defensive anchor up front.

"We are here because of the triangle, our culture, some great leadership, and some unbelievable gutsy kids that have made some unbelievable plays in the perfect timing," Traylor said. "That's what I'm hoping to see again."

The result is a team that has erased deficits in five wins this season, including a pair of double-digit comebacks.

Once again, the Roadrunners are earning votes as a top 25 team in the country despite ranking in the top 25 in hardly any statistical category.

"We may not have the best certain units, maybe defense or offense," cornerback RJ Lester said. "But all-around team, I think we're one of the better ones."

images.caption: UTSA Roadrunners head coach Jeff Traylor after the game against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News)

articles.title: NCAA penalizes No. 21 Liberty for tampering violations by 2 assistant coaches, staffer
articles.summary: 21 Liberty on a year of probation among penalties for tampering violations, including suspensions served earlier this year and show-cause orders for two assi...
articles.body:
LYNCHBURG, Va. (AP) — The NCAA has placed No. 21 Liberty on a year of probation among penalties for tampering violations, including suspensions served earlier this year and show-cause orders for two assistant coaches and a football staffer.

Assistant coaches Newland Isaac and Tony Washington, and general manager of player personnel Colton Korn all missed the Sept. 5 loss to James Madison. Washington also missed the Sept. 12 win against Gardner-Webb. All three received show-cause penalties that will block them from communicating with potential transfers through the January portal window, with Korn and Isaac at one year and Washington for two.

Additionally, head coach Jamey Chadwell served a one-week ban from recruiting communication in September under the provision that head coaches are responsible for conduct within their programs.

Those were among a list of penalties announced by the NCAA on Tuesday , tied to improper contact with two potential athletes and their representatives when they were still enrolled at Monmouth but had not yet entered the transfer portal. Specifically, the violations were tied to 89 text messages and six phone calls between Washington, Korn and Isaac combined.

The athletes ultimately didn't transfer to Liberty.

The penalties include a $25,000 fine, a three-week ban on all football recruiting communication for the 2026-27 academic year and a three-week ban on unofficial recruiting visits for 2026-27. They came after the school and enforcement staff went through the negotiated resolutions process used when parties agree on facts, level of violations and penalties as a way to streamline cases with no appeals.

Liberty (10-1) closes the regular season Saturday at Missouri State.

articles.title: Bolton Wanderers 1-3 West Bromwich Albion: Aune Heggebo nets twice in Baggies win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bolton Wanderers and West Bromwich Albion at the Toughsheet Community Stadium on Wednesday night; Aune Heggebo nets twice in Baggies win.
articles.body:
Hot-shot Heggebo gave James Morrison's in-form visitors a 21st-minute lead which was cancelled out by substitute Ruben Rodrigues' 63rd-minute penalty.

But West Brom, without injured top scorer Isaac Price, finished strongly, with Myhre's fifth goal since his summer move from Brann restoring Albion's lead after 75 minutes.

And Heggebo, back in the starting line-up after last Saturday's draw with Swansea, sealed a fifth win in eight unbeaten games with a penalty seven minutes from time.

It all added up to only Albion's second success at the Toughsheet Community Stadium since 2000.

The Baggies quickly imposed themselves on their hosts, fashioning a brace of early shooting opportunities.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu pushed away a third-minute Harry Whitwell effort and then kept out a low drive from Kareem Tunde.

Bolton have conceded more goals from crosses than any other Championship team this season, so it was little surprise to see Morrison's men exploit this weakness to take the lead.

Heggebo was involved in the build-up and then raced into the six-yard box to slide in Callum Styles' teasing centre from Bolton's right flank.

A slick training ground corner routine almost paid dividends for the Baggies after 37 minutes but the set-up proved better than Tunde's rising drive into the North Stand.

For all their domination, West Brom were almost caught out three minutes from half-time.

Former Baggies loanee Sam Iling-Junior ended a strong run with an inviting cross but Theo Bair - deputising for top scorer Sam Dalby - headed over. The Canadian striker then flicked another chance over the crossbar as Bolton finished the half strongly.

That was Bair's last action as he did not reappear for the second half, replaced by Dalby. Bolton also brought on defender Chris Forino and shortly afterwards swapped Xavier Simons for Rodrigues in a bid to get back into the contest.

Those changes did make a difference as Bolton levelled from the spot. George Campbell was adjudged to have handled Rodrigues' shot and the Portuguese midfielder drilled in his third goal of the season.

Iling-Junior had the ball in the net again eight minutes later but his celebrations were cut short by an assistant referee's flag.

The same player was then denied by Max O'Leary's fingertips after a stunning curling attempt with the outside of his boot.

Having survived the scare, West Brom imposed themselves once again, with Myhre and Heggebo taking them within three points of the top two.

"The lads did everything we asked of them at half-time by being braver and playing with more energy.

"But we wasted 40 minutes of the first half because we were not aggressive or tight enough.

"We spoke about how well West Brom pass the ball and they have good movement.

"So we couldn't afford to give them too much time and space, which they had in the first half.

"I felt it necessary to change at half-time and go more aggressive and change system.

"We were good for half-an-hour of the second half and were probably on top and then they got a second goal which was a blow.

"The third goal was another error, which was needless."

"I thought he (Heggebo) would be perfect for this game if we could get behind their high back line.

"We knew he would be in the space behind to arrive and be better suited in the box.

"Any team would miss big players and what they bring to the team. But it's not to cry about, it is about trying to find the best way and trust in the players who come in."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Burnley 0-2 Birmingham City: August Priske nets as Blues ease past struggling Clarets
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Burnley and Birmingham City at Turf Moor on Wednesday night; Clarets make it 24 winless games in a row at home in the league, the longest run in English Football League history.
articles.body:
It is now 24 games since the Clarets last celebrated three points in front of their own fans, a nightmare run that has now stretched to 403 days. It represents the worst sequence in the history of English football.

Burnley, relegated from the Premier League last season, remain firmly ensconced in the drop zone. Coach Fabio Celestini has picked up just three points in the five games he has taken charge off since succeeding Nicky Hayen last month and his team were jeered off at the end.

For City, however, it was a timely return to form following the 1-0 defeat at Stoke on Saturday. This was a seventh win in nine for Chris Davies' team and they are just two places and two points off the automatic promotion spots.

Burnley started on the front foot, with Aaron Ramsey forcing goalkeeper James Beadle into action with a low drive from 25 yards.

But the visitors went ahead in the seventh minute when James Stansfield was found in space by Carlos Vicente and his driven cross was diverted home by the sliding Priske. It was the Dane's eighth goal of the season.

The Clarets responded positively, with Largie Ramazani forcing Beadle into two smart saves and also having a shot deflected over. Zeki Amdouni also sent a decent chance too high.

Birmingham should have doubled their lead just before the break, but after Liam Millar had shaken off a couple of weak challenges, his shot lacked pace and precision and home keeper Max Weiss was able to save.

The visitors doubled their lead in the 52nd minute when Millar's inswinging corner from the right flicked off Banel's head and looped into the far corner of his own goal.

Priske saw the ball shave the post as he arrived under pressure from Max Alleyne to meet Bright Osayi-Samuel's cross as the visitors looked to turn the screw, with Burnley's fans beginning to voice their discontent.

The Clarets' only win this season came at Watford last month. They have now conceded 35 goals, the same number as bottom club Derby.

It needed a sprawling Weiss save to prevent defender Igor scoring the second own goal of the game when he sent an attempted chest pass towards the corner of the net before the keeper intervened.

Celestini sent on Jamie Vardy in an attempt to salvage something, only for fellow substitute Andreas Hountondji to see his shot saved by Beadle after breaking clear.

Birmingham could have scored again four minutes from time but Demarai Gray's penalty was saved by Weiss after he had been fouled by Alleyne.

"I understand the fans are frustrated. They have been waiting for a victory here for a long time. The reaction the fans showed is right at this moment, so it is head down and work harder.

"If they see some good things then they are with us 100 per cent, like they were at the start. They are frustrated but we have to change that.

"We lost the game because Birmingham were better than us in both boxes. In the 70 metres in the centre of the pitch, we were better than them. But they have one shot and score one goal and that made it very difficult.

"If we can be more efficient then I will be in absolutely no doubt about my team because I see good things. Tomorrow is another day and we must keep fighting.

"When I came here, it was clear that we would have to fight. This is not a surprise. But I really do see some good things."

"It was an excellent win. It was all about solidity, appetite and application.

"I am told this was our fifth away win, which was as many as we managed in the whole of last season, so that shows you something.

"I made a few changes and I think the balance I was trying to strike came to fruition. We scored twice and could have scored even more. We created some very good chances.

"I heard some of our fans had a problem on the M6. It took some of them three hours to get here on a freezing midweek night in the middle of winter.

"So it was good to play like that, get the win and send them home loud and proud and happy with their team."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Watford 0-1 Blackburn: Todd Cantwell penalty steers Rovers to victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Watford and Blackburn Rovers at Vicarage Road on Wednesday night; Todd Cantwell's penalty proves enough as Hornets end with 10 men.
articles.body:
The former Romania national team coach, who had just flown in after signing a contract of undisclosed length, was introduced to a sparsely-populated Vicarage Road, to polite applause, 10 minutes before kick-off.

On the evidence of Watford's third home defeat of the season, he will have his work cut out to steer them away from the Championship's relegation quicksands.

By the time Iordanescu slips into the cockpit at Derby on Saturday, he will be the sixth different head coach, including interims, to take charge of Watford in 2026 after Javi Gracia, Charlie Daniels, Ed Still, Alessio Dionisi and Adrian Mariappa, who was holding the fort here.

After a damaging night, he will start his reign in the dugout without two key defenders after Jordan Zemura's red card and captain Mattie Pollock's fifth booking of the campaign.

Mariappa revealed Iordanescu had given the players a "great speech and showed his passion" when meeting his new players in the dressing room.

But with manager Tony Mowbray having stepped back to address health issues last week, for long periods Rovers were assured and they deserved the points.

In an even first half, skipper Cantwell whipped a free-kick over the top from 25 yards and centre-back Hayden Carter was foiled by Pollock's last-ditch tackle after a dazzling, mazy run.

Iker Bravo's effort flew just wide as the home side replied, and on the stroke of half-time the Hornets wasted a golden opportunity to go in front.

Jayden Fevrier tripped Zemura, but from the resulting penalty Rovers goalkeeper Aynsley Pears sprawled low to his right to turn Bravo's spot-kick round a post.

Barely 60 seconds after the resumption, Pears' opposite number Federico Ravaglia made a sharp save to deny Oladapo Afolayan and the Watford goalkeeper also did well to smother Cantwell's stooping header.

But Rovers went in front from the game's second penalty after 57 minutes when Pollock brought down Afolayan - referee Steve Martin's decision was a formality - and Cantwell made no mistake.

Pollock's fifth yellow card of the season rules him out of Iordanescu's baptism in the dugout at Pride Park, and worse was to follow for the home side five minutes later.

Zemura, already cautioned in the first half for kicking the ball away, was sent off for a second booking when he appealed for another penalty but was punished for alleged simulation.

Blackburn dominated the last half-hour and only Ravaglia's series of saves denied them a more comfortable win.

Watford's acting head coach Adrian Mariappa:

"The boys have to keep believing. They showed determination, they didn't roll over. These are the fine margins of football and at the moment we are falling the wrong side of those margins.

"We've got to keep working on the training pitch - that's how you get the rub of the green. We've got some big players to come back and it's just a question of putting the squad together and pushing on.

"The new coach has a great track record, a lot of experience and now everyone has to dig in together."

Blackburn's nterim head coach Damien Johnson:

"We want Tony to take comfort and pleasure iin results like that but we also hope he's getting the time and space he needs.

"Even when the game was 11 v 11, I thought we were the better side. This is the thing Tony has created - he has asked the guys to take ownership, and take more responsibility for their performances, so we didn't have too say much to the players at half-time.

"The only frustration was probably that we didn't capitalise on the opportunities we had to win by more, but it's not always easy when you are playing against 10 men. In the end it felt quite comfortable."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Stoke City 2-1 Millwall: Potters beat Lions to make it five wins a in row
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Stoke City and Millwall at the bet365 Stadium on Wednesday night; George Hirst scores twice as the in-form Potters beat the Lions.
articles.body:
The Scotland international scored just his second goal for the Potters in the 1-0 win over Birmingham on Saturday and doubled his tally for the season to take Stoke back into the automatic promotion places.

Mark Sykes' stunning strike halved the deficit in the final 10 minutes, but Stoke held on to claim an 11th win in their last 14 outings.

The defeat was Millwall's fourth in a row, coming a day after it was announced they had been ordered to play a future match in front of a partially closed stadium for offensive chanting.

Millwall had lost each of their last three league outings without scoring but it was the Lions who created the first chance within the first two minutes.

Tairyk Arconte broke the offside trap and latched on to Camiel Neghli's pass before bursting away down the right and forcing Viktor Johansson to push his low effort away from goal.

Stoke welcomed back star midfielder Ethan Galbraith from illness and the former Manchester United midfielder's spectacular volley crashed against the bar in an exhilarating opening five minutes.

Millwall manager Alex Neil, who was sacked by the Potters in December 2023, could only watch as Jack McGlynn's defence-splitting pass found Hirst, who steadied himself before picking out the bottom corner in the 13th minute.

McGlynn, Stoke's top scorer in the league this season, almost turned from provider to scorer when his long-range shot whistled past the upright.

Stoke had been good value for their lead and grabbed a second five minutes before half-time. Million Manhoef had also been recalled to the starting line-up and was allowed time and space in the Millwall box before picking out Hirst to turn into the corner.

Neil made a hat-trick of changes as the Lions set about trying to get back into the clash.

One of the reinforcements, top scorer Lyndon Dykes, arrowed a long throw into the Stoke box inside the first minute of the second half, which was kept alive by Neghli before fellow substitute Kyrell Lisbie headed goalwards.

Millwall offered much more of a threat after the break as the Potters came under their first sustained pressure of the evening.

Lisbie scuffed his shot when the ball broke kindly to him in the area and Dykes wasn't able to get to the follow-up. Alfie Doughty then saw his powerful effort blocked by Ben Johnson and the rebound was blazed over by Derek Mazou-Sacko.

Stoke earned some respite at the other end when Bae Jun-ho earned a free-kick for the hosts in a dangerous position, which McGlynn forced Lukas Jensen to push to safety.

Stoke manager Mark Robins brought on Sam Gallagher and Robert Bozenik in a double change in attack, and the pair combined for what should have been a Stoke third when Bozenik shot wide after Gallagher's clever cut back.

Millwall halved the deficit with nine minutes remaining as Sykes drifted infield and rifled his left-footed effort beyond Johansson from distance, but Stoke held on to keep their winning run on track.

"There's been a little bit said about George that is unfair. I think people want to see him working hard and I think he overthought things.

"It's amazing if you just remember that you love playing football and you just go and do it, and everything else tends to fall into place. It's not as simple as that but it really helps, and he's done that.

"First half was everything I thought we'd be. I thought we were good, we moved the ball well, we looked dangerous every time we had it.

"What we didn't do in the second half was get close to them at the top end of the pitch and that's sometimes when you tire in a game.

"You want your players to not sit in and invite the inevitable but you can't do that. The players will need to learn and understand what happened in the game. You can't rest on your laurels and see the game out.

"Go back to what happened on Saturday when we were down to 10 men, you don't do the same thing, we've got 11 men, matched in numbers and you've got to go and make things happen for yourself and we didn't do that.

"We weren't clinical enough, we didn't make the right choices in the second half, we had two really clear-cut chances. That was the disappointment."

"First half I didn't think we played with enough belief, enough quality, enough understanding. I thought we lacked loads of things in the first half.

"I thought we got into some good areas and I thought we got into some good pockets but we didn't really do anything as if we believed we were going to score a goal.

"The two goals we conceded were shocking. First half we lacked everything a Millwall team should be, we lacked aggression, intensity, we didn't get close enough.

"Their two lads in the middle of the pitch controlled the game, they were comfortable. The centre backs ate our forwards up.

"It was vastly improved in the second half, but in my opinion it's easy to play a game when you're losing 2-0, to go out and show a little bit more than you showed in the first half.

"We had three or four players in the game that took part, and they showed a bit of personality on the pitch, there was too many hoping that something was going to happen rather than believing you can go and influence a game.

"We had three fresh air shots in the box where the ball comes across and we miss the ball. You can talk about intensity, duels, running, but you also need quality. And if you don't have enough quality, this is a difficult league to win enough games in."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Liverpool transfer news: Sidy Barhama Ndiaye agrees deal to sign for Reds - Paper Talk

articles.body:
Liverpool have agreed a deal to sign highly-rated Senegalese wonderkid Sidy Barhama Ndiaye - The Sun

articles.title: Wyoming Suspends HC Jay Sawvel, Negotiations with NCAA Ongoing After Rules Violations
articles.summary: Wyoming head coach Jay Sawvel will not be on the sideline for Saturday's regular-season finale against UConn after the school announced Wednesday he was suspended one game.
articles.body:
Wyoming head coach Jay Sawvel will not be on the sideline for Saturday's regular-season finale against UConn after the school announced Wednesday he was suspended one game.

The announcement explained the suspension came as the school works with the NCAA enforcement staff and "in response to NCAA rules violations related to impermissible communication with prospective student-athletes and their representatives last December (2025)."

According to the statement, the seven athletes were still enrolled at other schools and yet to officially enter the transfer portal when the communication occurred even though they had "publicly announced (via social media) their intention to transfer."

Wyoming explained it self-reported the rules violations and is still working through "the negotiated resolution process" with the NCAA.

Defensive ends coach Brian Hendricks will be the head coach against UConn.

The Cowboys are 7-4 on the season and enter Saturday's game with plenty of momentum after winning five of the last six. Their only loss in that stretch was a seven-point defeat to 9-2 New Mexico.

This is Sawvel's third season as the head coach. While he went a combined 7-17 in his first two seasons, the team has shown significant improvement in 2026 and is bowl eligible for the first time since 2023.

articles.title: Club Brugge 0-3 Liverpool: Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz on target in dominant Champions League win
articles.summary: Report as Liverpool overpowered Club Brugge in Belgium with two goals from Alexander Isak and a fine strike from Florian Wirtz; Andoni Iraola's side rise to fifth in the Champions League phase standings, in prime position to finish inside the automatic qualifying spots
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola's side have had no problem scoring goals in Europe, but faced issues keeping them out. Brugge were most obliging hosts in that respect, a far cry from the regularly free-scoring side that have so far averaged 2.75 goals per game and beaten Inter Milan at the San Siro.

Felix Lemarechal was the home side's greatest threat. But Alexander Isak was far more decisive, netting the opener following Yann Sommer's misplaced pass before rounding off the scoring in the second half with a deft chip to beat the goalkeeper. Sandwiched between was a superb strike from the in-form Florian Wirtz, set up by a surging run from Rio Ngumoha.

Brugge got better, Lemarechal twice forced Alisson into saves and Nicolo Tresoldi, who has scored the same number of Champions League goals as Erling Haaland this term, also called the Brazilian into action. But Liverpool were creatively superior. Momentum is building.

Isak has now scored in six consecutive away outings for Liverpool while Wirtz continues to grow in stature and influence. The German has scored six times for club and country in the month of November alone. 12 points from five games gives the Reds a favourable chance of finishing inside the automatic qualifying positions, while Brugge drop to 13th - the first time they have tasted defeat in 11 games.

Wirtz hitting new heights in settled role

Florian Wirtz was, very briefly, the most expensive transfer in Premier League history when he joined Liverpool nearly 18 months ago. Only now is the German playmaker showing he was worth the record outlay.

His goal in Brugge marked a small but significant milestone, the first time he has scored in three consecutive appearances as a Liverpool player. It's been two years since the 23-year-old managed to find such consistency of output.

Wirtz's brilliance extended beyond his goal, linking play through the thirds and igniting attacks without relinquishing control out of possession. Finally, Iraola appears to have found a formula that brings the best out of the midfielder's qualities.

Here is a moment where the headline numbers have finally caught up with his growing influence.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola to TNT Sports:

"It was very positive. It puts us in a good position. We want to go to the top eight. We were efficient, a more difficult game than it looks now.

"It was difficult to expect a clean sheet, we expected an open game, man to man, so overall a very good performance. I appreciate a lot this win."

On Isak: "As a team, I value the first goal, but the second goal was also very nice."

Liverpool forward Alexander Isak to TNT Sports:

"It was a perfect away win, I would say.

"I feel good, I'm in a good place, the team is in a good place most importantly.

"That's where we want to be, and hopefully it just gets better from here."

articles.title: Ancelotti y Mbappé le complican la vida al Bayern
articles.standfirst: El Lille remonta el gol de Upamecano, gana su primer partido y llena de dudas a los alemanes
articles.summary: El Lille remonta el gol de Upamecano, gana su primer partido y llena de dudas a los alemanes
articles.body: El Bayern está en un momento extraño. En lugar de música bávara y cerveza, a su alrededor se escucha ruido y se bebe vinagre. Las lesiones, la baja de Kompany y la situación de Musiala forman una densa niebla en torno al conjunto muniqués que está afectando a sus resultados. El top 8 de la Copa de Europa parece lejano. Con un once lleno de suplentes; el Bayern se plantó en Lille a ganar por inercia y por las dudas de un rival metido en la parte baja de la clasificación. Y casi le sale bien. Upamecano adelantó a los alemanes al cabecear un córner en el que Özer reclamó falta en ataque. Los de Davide Ancelotti, en vez de venirse abajo, llenaron la mochila y la cantimplora y se lanzaron hacia la ruta de la remontada. Ueda buscó un atajo, pero su 1-1 no subió al marcador porque había cometido falta sobre Kimmich. En vez de rematar el balón golpeó la pantorrilla del rival. El japonés aprendió la lección y en la siguiente no falló. Nathan Ngoy se lanzó en expedición y asistió a Ueda, que desafió las leyes de la biomecánica con un giro de tobillo magnífico para mandar la bola al palo largo, lejos del alcance de Urbig. El gol fue un chute de moral para el Lille, que empezó a encontrar huecos en un Bayern asustado y, tres minutos después del 1-1, llegó el segundo del equipo del norte de Francia en una acción incomprensible de Pavlovic. Ethan Mbappé corrió al espacio, se plantó ante el portero y le superó con la definición, pero el balón se estrelló en el palo y fue a parar a los dominios de Pavlovic... que despejó hacia su propia portería. El Bayern se lanzó al área rival, pero no fue capaz de encontrar situaciones claras de remate. Con ocho puntos en cinco jornadas se queda a mitad de tabla y con urgencias si quiere entrar entre los ocho primeros. En Lille, por fin, alegría de Champions. Hay tiempo para soñar con meterse el playoff. Poco tiempo, pero hay.

articles.title: Sporting 2-2 Man Utd: Mauricio Pochettino denied first win by Senne Lammens howler in Champions League
articles.summary: Report as Man Utd self-destruct in bizarre Champions League draw at Sporting after having two goals controversially ruled out; Bruno Fernandes and Luis Suarez both scored two goals, one penalty each, with the Man Utd captain's second goal freakishly bouncing in off a divot in the ground
articles.body:
United looked to be on course for a first away win of the season after captain Bruno Fernandes scored two goals in the first five minutes of the second half only for Lammens to spill the ball in the box for Luis Suarez to equalise with his second goal of the game.

Pochettino thought United had gone back in front for a second time shortly after Lammens' error when Sporting goalkeeper Kaique punched into his own net at a corner. However, it was ruled out following an on-field review for a foul by substitute Patrick Dorgu.

It was a damaging night for Lammens, who gave away the penalty for Suarez's first goal just 75 seconds after saving the Sporting striker's poorly taken spot-kick. The man brought into replace the error-prone Andre Onana is now beginning to resemble his predecessor.

Fernandes' equaliser three minutes after the restart came from the third penalty of what was a bizarre match. Few moments topped the United skipper's freakish second goal which came thanks a tame effort bouncing up off a divot in the ground and into back of the net.

Tielemans' stoppage-time red will only add to United's frustrations. It was his first booking, for a tame follow-through on Goncalo Inacio, that denied Amad Diallo from equalising late in the first half in one of the more baffling refereeing decisions you will see.

Pochettino's first two matches have seen his side have two players sent off and concede two penalties. If he did not know it before, he certainly knows now that nothing comes easy at United, who sit 19th in the Champions League and Premier League.

Were Man Utd hard done by to have two goals ruled out?

The last thing Pochettino needed after the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool - and Leny Yoro's now overturned red card - was more refereeing controversy. However, there was contention around both goals United had ruled out in Lisbon.

Amad had the ball in the back of the net toward the end of the first half to equalise - but not before the whistle had gone for what was judged to have been a foul by Tielemans, who clearly won the ball with his slide tackle.

The United midfielder received a booking for his follow through on Sporting defender Inacio, who went down dramatically despite receiving the slightest of contact. VAR could not intervene as the whistle had gone.

"It is a terrible decision," said Sky Sports pundit Clinton Morrison. "Tielemans won the ball."

United's second disallowed goal, which was ruled out following VAR intervention, saw Dorgu penalised for making contact with Sporting goalkeeper Kaique before he punched into his own net.

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher felt it was "very harsh" for the referee to disallow the goal after being sent to his monitor.

Carra: Man Utd 'unlucky' but Lammens error can't happen

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher to CBS:

"I do think United were a little bit unlucky tonight with the goal disallowed just before half-time. The goal at the end felt very harsh to me, the one where it could have been 3-2...

"The focus on a Man Utd goalkeeper is always big if he's making mistakes. The back-ups aren't even at the level where you could say no matter how poorly the goalkeeper plays, you could change it. You worry about the confidence of that goalkeeper now.

"That mistake for the equaliser, the 2-2 goal, you say sometimes 'an amateur goalkeeper wouldn't make that mistake' and that just can't happen at this level."

Man Utd head coach Mauricio Pochettino to TNT Sports :

"I'm so proud of the players. It was a tough game. I liked the team we played for 90 minutes, the personality, the character. It's difficult to find a game where you get punished in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions. Today we showed how we want to play after just one week of working together.

"We need to concentrate and focus more, try to recover better. The performance like today's is the best medicine to prepare for the next game."

29: PENALTY TO SPORTING! Martinez fouls Catamo to give Sporting a spot-kick.

31: LAMMENS SAVES IT! Man Utd are spared as Suarez's poor effort is saved by the Belgian.

32: ANOTHER PENALTY TO SPORTING! Seventy-five seconds later, Lammens fouls Araujo in the box to go from hero to zero.

33: GOAL FOR SPORTING! Suarez makes no mistake from his second penalty.

40: NO GOAL! Amad thinks he's levelled for Man Utd but the referee had blown for a foul by Tielemans, who is shown a yellow card.

47: PENALTY TO MAN UTD! Martinez is brought down by Quaresma in the box to give his side a lifeline.

48: GOAL FOR MAN UTD! Fernandes brings his side level from the spot.

50: ANOTHER MAN UTD GOAL! Fernandes scores a freak goal as his soft shot bounces off a divot in the ground and into the back of the net.

80: GOAL FOR SPORTING! A howler from Lammens sees him spill the ball for Suarez to equalise.

82: GOAL FOR MAN UTD! Sporting goalkeeper Kaique punches the ball into his own net at a corner.

84: GOAL DISALLOWED! Referee rules that Dorgu fouled the goalkeeper after VAR sent him to his monitor.

articles.title: Pochettino cosecha un punto en un debut europeo con mucha polémica
articles.standfirst: Sendos dobletes de Luis Suárez y Bruno Fernandes ponen las tablas en el marcador
articles.summary: Sendos dobletes de Luis Suárez y Bruno Fernandes ponen las tablas en el marcador
articles.body: Partido polémico en Lisboa, con un punto para cada equipo en el debut europeo de Mauricio Pochettino, que pudo rescatar un empate gracias a los dos goles de Bruno Fernandes. Y pudieron ser tres si no llega a anular el árbitro Marciniak el 2-3 en el 82'. Muy protestado por los 'mancunianos'. El partido empezó con una primera parte en la que pasaron cosas, y todas en contra del United. Lo primero, dos penaltis marcados por el polaco Marciniak y lanzados ambos por el colombiano Luis Suárez. El primero, por falta de Lisandro, fue parado por Lammens (seguía el 0-0); y el segundo, hecho por el propio Lammens en una falsa salida, fue convertido por el ariete del Sporting (era el 1-0 en el minuto 32') en su quinto gol, entonces, en cinco partidos de Champions. No todo quedó ahí. En el 39', una dudosa falta en ataque propició que a Diallo le anularan el 1-1. Una decisión muy controvertida de Marciniak (la falta no pareció existir) que provocó que el partido se fuera 1-0 al descanso, con un United que quizá no mereció ese castigo. El Sporting, con los españoles Fresneda y Altimira titulares, podía con un United con Zirkzee de ariete... hasta que apareció Bruno Fernandes (ex del Sporting). El 1-1 vino en un penalti dudoso provocado por Lisando. Lo marcó Bruno. Y el 1-2, dos minutos más tarde, en un disparo inofensivo de Bruno que votó en un hoyo (literal) y se tragó el brasileño Kaique Pereira, meta lisboeta. Cuatro goles de Bruno en cinco choques de CL. Y a partir de ahí, vino más polémica. Primero, con el empate del Sporting, en una posible falta a Lammens, (no la pitó Marciniak) que Luis Suárez (seis goles y máximo goleador del torneo) metió de tijera a puerta vacía; y luego en el posible 2-3, que anuló Marciniak por falta (existente) al meta local del Sporting. Así se quedó la cosa: 2-2... y alegría para ninguno, con Tielemans expulsado en el 92'.

articles.title: Lautaro reaparece y devuelve la alegría al Inter
articles.standfirst: Regresó a los terrenos de juego en la Liga de Campeones más de un mes después de su lesión
articles.summary: Regresó a los terrenos de juego en la Liga de Campeones más de un mes después de su lesión
articles.body: El argentino Lautaro Martínez, capitán y héroe del Inter de Milan, volvió a ver puerta ante el Stuttgart tras regresar a los terrenos de juego en la Liga de Campeones más de un mes después de su lesión, y se sumó al gol de Luka Sucic para sellar una victoria de mucha importancia para su equipo. El conjunto dirigido por Cristian Chivu comenzó con dificultades ante la presión del Stuttgart, que avisó en los primeros minutos. Poco a poco carburó y se acercó al área rival con la dupla Marcus Thuram y Pio Esposito, y con el argentino, líder del equipo, en el banquillo tras volver a jugar el domingo después de sufrir una distensión muscular en los flexores del muslo izquierdo. Los locales buscaron, insistentes, un primer gol que no llegó durante los primeros cuarenta y cinco minutos debido a la eficacia defensiva de los alemanes, que neutralizaron al Inter, sobre todo en los últimos metros. En el minuto 40, Alessandro Bastoni tuvo que abandonar el terreno de juego por unas molestias musculares en la pierna izquierda. Federico Dimarco entró en su lugar para cubrir la baja del central italiano. Antes del paso por vestuarios, el conjunto milanés intensificó su presión y rozó el gol en dos ocasiones consecutivas. Primero, Thuram aprovechó un error defensivo para quedarse cerca de Seimen, pero su disparo se marchó fuera. Poco después, Barella recibió un pase de Pio Esposito y estrelló el balón en el poste. La segunda mitad comenzó con el Stuttgart dispuesto a buscar el gol. Nikolas Nartey avisó en el minuto 46 con un disparo desde la frontal que se marchó ligeramente por encima del larguero, y el Inter respondió a balón parado, con una falta de Dimarco que el guardameta despejó cuando Akanji esperaba para rematar. El Inter encontró entonces la oportunidad de adelantarse después de que Vagnoman desviara con el brazo un centro de Dimarco. El árbitro, tras revisar la acción en el monitor a instancias del VAR, señaló penalti. Sucic asumió la responsabilidad desde los once metros en el minuto 57 y no falló. El equipo 'neroazzurri' buscó ampliar la ventaja. Lo hizo posible a través de Lautaro Martínez, que, tras su lesión en el muslo izquierdo a medidados de octubre, tiene, de nuevo, hambre de gol. Jugó doce minutos el pasado domingo ante el Atalanta, y hoy solo le valieron cinco para hacer lo que mejor se le da. Meter goles. En el minuto 74, Dimarco puso un centro al área, Pio Esposito dejó pasar el balón con un inteligente movimiento y Lautaro apareció para conectar un disparo con la derecha que superó a Seimen y estableció el 2-0. Fue el tercer tanto del argentino en la Liga de Campeones esta temporada y el séptimo en el curso. El Inter supo gestionar el tramo final para cerrar una victoria importante, con la que empieza a compensar las dos derrotas encajadas en las primeras jornadas de la Liga de Campeones. Los de Chivu encadenan ahora tres triunfos consecutivos.

articles.title: Man United denied at Sporting as referee overshadows Fernandes double
articles.summary: Bruno Fernandes nets twice in Lisbon, but referee’s decisions in spotlight as Mauricio Pochettino denied first win.
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino must wait for his first win as Manchester United coach, after a wild 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, with the hosts equalising thanks to a goalkeeping error from Senne Lammens.

The Belgian stopper’s poor handling allowed Luis Suarez to complete a brace for the hosts, cancelling out United playmaker Bruno Fernandes’s double against his former side.

United gave away two penalties in the first half, the second converted by Suarez, before Fernandes equalised from the spot early in the second half.

Fernandes sent United ahead with a lucky bounce taking his effort over the Sporting goalkeeper, before Suarez’s acrobatic effort levelled the game.

United midfielder Youri Tielemans was sent off in stoppage time for a second yellow card to end a compelling and often erratic match.

A crushing 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend, leaving United 19th, was a disastrous first game at the helm for Pochettino after replacing Michael Carrick.

Pochettino brought Harry Maguire into the three-man defence as he shuffled his pack, as well as starting Joshua Zirkzee in place of the suspended Matheus Cunha.

Neither side took many risks in the opening stages, with few chances of note until the game burst into life midway through the first half as United lost control.

Lisandro Martinez brought down Geny Catamo in the area and Sporting were awarded a penalty.

The hosts blew their chance from the spot, with Suarez’s scuffed effort easily saved by Lammens, but the Red Devils gave away another spot kick just a couple of minutes later.

Goalkeeper Lammens came flying off his line and clattered Maxi Araujo, and this time Colombian striker Suarez made no mistake from the spot.

Manchester United unhappy with disallowed goals

United thought they had equalised when Amad Diallo hit the crossbar and then nodded home the rebound, but the goal was disallowed to their dismay.

Youri Tielemans was ruled to have fouled Goncalo Inacio, although he seemed to win the ball, upsetting United further after Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool on Sunday that was later rescinded.

Fernandes pulled United level early in the second half from the spot after Eduardo Quaresma brought down Martinez.

The former Sporting playmaker calmly stroked his penalty beyond the dive of Kaique Pereira into the bottom left corner.

Fernandes said on the eve of the game he had stopped contract talks because he wanted to focus on helping United improve their form after a dire start to the season.

The midfielder soon had his second goal, with the help of a bizarre bounce off a divot on the pitch.

Fernandes’s low effort from distance seemed bound for Pereira’s hands, but suddenly bounced up off a patch of uneven turf and fortuitously over the goalkeeper’s head.

The Portugal international bent a free-kick narrowly off target as he looked to complete his hat-trick.

Lammens saved well from Sergi Altimira to protect United’s lead as Sporting battled to find an equaliser.

It eventually came from a howler from Lammens, who failed to claim a cross dropping out of the sky, spilling the ball in front of Suarez, who produced a hooked acrobatic effort to score.

Moments later United had the ball in the net at the other end after another goalkeeping error by Pereira, who mishandled Fernandes’s corner, pushing the ball into his own net.

However, what would have been the winner was disallowed for an elbow by Patrick Dorgu on the goalkeeper, a decision the visitors were also unhappy about.

articles.title: Malen and Roma deny injury-hit PSG in Champions League draw
articles.summary: Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain held to 2-2 draw by Roma as injury-ravaged squad struggle.
articles.body:
Donyell Malen’s penalty gave Roma a 2-2 draw away to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday, as the injury-hit reigning champions saw their perfect record in this season’s competition come to an end.

Malen stroked in from the spot in the 78th minute on a bitterly cold and wet night at the Parc des Princes, giving Roma a welcome point after their collapse from two goals up to lose 3-2 at Manchester United last time out.

Roma had earlier taken the lead through Mario Hermoso, only for Illia Zabarnyi to equalise before substitute Ousmane Dembele put PSG briefly in front with a penalty of his own.

The result ends PSG’s perfect record in this season’s league phase, and halts a run of 12 consecutive wins in all competitions for Luis Enrique’s team.

They fall two points behind Real Madrid, who are now clear at the top of the standings as the only side still with a 100 percent record after five matches.

It is only a minor setback for PSG in their quest to finish in the top eight of the 36-team table, and therefore qualify directly for the last 16 without having to go through the playoff round like in the last two campaigns.

But the Parisians could have done with the boost of a victory as they come to terms with the loss of the outstanding Desire Doue, who may not play again this season after rupturing the ACL in his right knee last weekend.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, another of their outstanding attacking players, recently succumbed to the same injury, while Dembele has been struggling for fitness, too, and PSG’s prospects of winning a third straight Champions League title are undoubtedly diminished as a result.

Dembele’s presence on the bench at kickoff meant that none of PSG’s five top scorers from last season was in their line-up here, with the others either injured or having departed in the case of Bradley Barcola and Goncalo Ramos.

Meanwhile, Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini raised eyebrows by leaving Malen out of his starting XI. The Dutchman is running at an average of more than a goal a game this season and netted four against Parma last weekend.

However, Roma have been in prolific form in general, netting 26 goals in their last seven matches before arriving in the French capital.

They went ahead inside five minutes here as Matias Soule cut the ball back from the byline and Spanish defender Hermoso was on hand to convert.

Roma had blown even more promising leads already this season, though, losing 4-3 at home to Real Madrid after leading 3-1 with eight minutes left, and then going down 3-2 at Old Trafford despite being 2-0 ahead at half-time.

Ukrainian defender Zabarnyi levelled just after the half-hour mark as he found space at the near post to head in Senny Mayulu’s corner.

Evan Ndicka headed just off-target for Roma late in the first half, and Niccolo Pisilli forced a good stop from Matvei Safonov early in the second half.

Joao Neves then headed agonisingly wide for PSG as he arrived unmarked in the area to meet a Nuno Mendes cross, before Dembele was introduced for the hosts in place of the ineffective Ferran Torres.

Moments after that, PSG won a penalty when Achraf Hakimi stormed into the Roma box only to be pulled down by Wesley.

The French side had missed four penalties in the Champions League since the start of last season, but Dembele did score in the final against Arsenal in May.

He kept a cool head to convert his fifth goal of the campaign, but PSG could not make it five straight Champions League wins this season.

Malen entered the fray for Roma midway through the second half and looked on as Dembele was denied a brilliant solo goal by a Mile Svilar save.

Roma then won a penalty following a VAR check after Vitinha blocked a Soule shot with a raised hand in the box.

Up stepped Malen to score his 17th goal of a prolific campaign, boosting Roma’s hopes of reaching the knockout phase.

articles.body: Diego Pablo Simeone atendió a los medios tras la segunda victoria rojiblanca en esta Champions frente al Viking. Nos ayuda en diferentes facetas, ojalá nos siga ayudando porque lo necesitamos. Koke cada vez mejor Difícil explicar algo que gusta verlo. Cuando está en el campo el trato de balón es diferencial, tiene una personalidad que se hace dueño del partido. Es difícil verle errar un pase. Empieza a tener más años, por eso le dosificamos, pero terminó haciendo un partido más de forma increíble. El mejor regalo que se llevó fue el cariño de la gente. Julián, si en lo personal le puede afectar los pitos Estoy feliz con él. Lo quiero como persona, le voy a sostener como futbolista, no hay una jugada que no pase por él. No tengo dudas de que para llegar donde queremos necesitamos al mejor Julián. Resumen Primera parte muy buena. También tuvieron ellos el 2-1, nosotros también. En el segundo controlamos menos el juego, pero con menos ocasiones y menos calidad que en el primero. Trabajamos para que se equilibre el primer tiempo con el segundo. La aportación de Hancko, que no tiene tanto foco Para nosotros es una pieza muy importante, puede jugar de tercero, de lateral, de segundo... Tiene gol, pie importante, es muy completo. Va en crecimiento continuo. Desde que llegó hay un crecimiento y ojalá siga creciendo. Está en esa faceta de crecimiento puro. Recuperar confianza tras las dos derrotas Nunca perdimos la confianza. Ellos fueron contundentes, pero no cambiamos el paso ni la seguridad ni el camino que estamos teniendo. Viking Equipo valiente, que presiona bien en campo rival. Hicimos un partido muy bueno, logramos hundirlos, nos vamos con una victoria importante en el día de hoy. Qué necesita el Viking en Champions Soy muy respetuoso con el rival y con el entrenador. No me permitiría decir en qué tienen que mejorar.

articles.title: 'Disgrace' decisions, divots and howlers - Man Utd chaos against Sporting
articles.summary: BBC Sport breaks down the chaos amid Manchester United's rollercoaster Champions League draw against Sporting in Lisbon.
articles.body:
Manchester United were held to a draw in a chaotic and controversial Champions League encounter with Sporting in Lisbon with Mauricio Pochettino denied a first win as United head coach despite his side turning around a first-half deficit.

They were behind at the break after goalkeeper Senne Lammens conceded from a penalty he gave away – having saved another just minutes before.

United then had a goal disallowed before scoring a penalty of their own through Bruno Fernandes, who then put them in front with the help of a large divot on the pitch.

There was more drama as Lammens dropped the ball for Sporting's equaliser before Pochettino's side had what they thought was a winner ruled out.

Polish referee Szymon Marciniak was at the centre of much of the drama with midfielder Youri Tielemans sent off in stoppage time.

BBC Sport breaks down each incident after a crazy night.

Lammens saved a poor penalty from Sporting's Luis Suarez, given after Lisandro Martinez left a leg out which caught Geny Catamo.

The Belgium keeper got down to hold on to Suarez's low effort which looked set to be a huge boost for the underperforming United number one.

Pochettino's whirlwind week ends with optimism and frustration

Lammens went from hero to zero in the space of 76 seconds as he rushed out of his goal and took out Maxi Araujo in the United box.

Noussair Mazraoui was caught out by a ball over the top but it was reckless from Lammens and this time Suarez buried the spot-kick.

Former United midfielder Owen Hargreaves told TNT Sports: "There is no way Senne Lammens can get there. Just stay in the goal."

Amad Diallo thought he had equalised for United before half-time when he headed in after his first attempted was turned on to the cross bar.

However, referee Marciniak blew his whistle for a foul against Youri Tielemans.

Replays showed Tielemans won the ball and pulled out of the challenge after he played the ball through to Amad.

BBC Sport's Dale Johnson: "Marciniak believed that Goncalo Inacio had been fouled by Youri Tielemens on the edge of the area as the Manchester United midfielder played a pass through.

"Rather than immediately blow his whistle, Marciniak held off to let the move play out.

"But when Diallo hit the bar with his first effort, Marciniak blew his whistle.

"Play was dead at that point, so when Diallo then nodded the rebound over the line the VAR was locked out.

"However, the chances that the VAR would have intervened were very slim.

"Tielemens, who was booked, caught Inacio's foot under his body sliding to make the pass, causing the Sporting defender's ankle to buckle."

Former Manchester United midfielder Ashley Young said on BBC Radio 5 Live: "It's an absolute disgrace. I don't know how the referee is seeing that Tielemans has kicked the player.

"On first viewing, I thought his foot must have hit him on the follow through but when you look at it again, Tielemans actually tries to take his foot away.

"He doesn't touch him because he knows the midfielder is coming towards him.

"It is one of the worst decisions I've seen with a referee giving that decision."

United got back on level terms after a foul on Martinez in the Sporting area by Eduardo Quaresma led to a penalty. Bruno Fernandes converted.

Former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha told BBC Sport: "Martinez wins that penalty, but it is a penalty."

United took the lead with two quick-fire goals but in bizarre circumstances as Fernandes' speculative strike looked like it would be easily collected by Kaique Pereira only to hit a divot on the pitch and fly up past the Sporting goalkeeper.

Former Rangers striker Ally McCoist on TNT Sports: "I think it hits a divot and it jumps over the goalkeeper! That is absolutely incredible."

Hargreaves added on TNT Sports: "Unbelievable. It is like a golf divot. There are holes in this pitch absolutely everywhere.

"Bruno Fernandes created a divot, does he get an assist for that?"

Lammens howler gifts equaliser (80 mins)

Lammens made another error, spilling a high ball under little pressure from Suarez. The Sporting striker then reacted quickly to find the target with an overhead kick to make it 2-2, the goal given after a quick VAR check.

McCoist: "I am baffled because the forward does what you expect him to do.

"The goalkeeper, instead of concentrating on the ball, he thinks about the player."

United thought they had taken the lead as Sporting keeper Kaique appeared to push the ball into his own net from a Fernandes corner.

However, after a VAR intervention, the 'goal' was then disallowed for a foul on the goalkeeper by Patrick Dorgu.

Onuoha: "First that was an absolutely disastrous goal for United to concede for the equaliser. it comes from a nothing ball into the box, too.

"For the United goal that has just been ruled out, the keeper has pushed it into his own net before Dorgu has touched him."

Young added on BBC Radio 5 Live: "The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me.

"If a referee is on the pitch and being sent to the screen, if he's given the goal then stand by your decision."

Midfielder Tielemans was then sent off for a late challenge on Sergi Altimira. The Belgium international's second yellow compounds the controversial one he received in the first half.

United have now received five red cards in all competitions this season - two more than any other Premier League side.

Young added: "The referee's performance was just simply 'wow'.

"The decisions that he gave. Youri Tielemans getting booked to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking and it should have been an equalising goal.

"His decision-making today is nothing more than a disgrace."

articles.title: Man Utd on wrong end of more controversial decisions in Sporting draw
articles.summary: What are the findings for Mauricio Pochettino after his first two matches as Manchester United manager?
articles.body:
Two games, no wins. Two red cards, two goals scored. One goal disallowed, six conceded. Is it possible for Mauricio Pochettino to have learned anything from a crazy first week as Manchester United boss?

United and Pochettino went on the warpath before the Champions League encounter with Sporting, furious at Leny Yoro's dismissal at Liverpool which they believe was unjust and shaped the eventual 4-0 defeat.

Club officials were seething after the 2-2 draw in Lisbon as well.

This time it was 2022 World Cup final referee Szymon Marciniak in the firing line. Blowing before Amad's first-half header went into the net meant VAR had no chance to assess whether the Polish official was right to rule Youri Tielemans had fouled Goncalo Inacio before prodding the ball through to the Ivorian.

Former United winger Ashley Young didn't think so. He called Marciniak's performance "a disgrace".

That Tielemans picked up a booking that eventually led to his late red card – the Old Trafford outfit have now had four players sent off in their past five games, meaning the Belgian will miss the Old Trafford clash with RB Leipzig on 8 December - just compounded the situation.

Then, in a matter of minutes, Marciniak decided neither Manchester United keeper Senne Lammens nor Sporting counterpart Kaique had been fouled as they conceded. Their respective defences complained bitterly. Marciniak was only asked to go to the pitchside monitor by VAR for the latter incident, which he overturned.

United insiders felt the Tielemans incident was clearly not a foul and Amad's goal should have stood. They also felt any foul on Kaique by Patrick Dorgu was marginal and did not warrant their goal being disallowed.

Pochettino trod a fine path, knowing if he said something too controversial, it could land him with a fine.

A nod of a head in agreement was his initial reaction in his post-match news conference, when asked if he felt Marciniak had got it wrong.

A few minutes before, he was more expansive when he spoke to TNT.

"It's difficult to find a game where you get punished [so much] in one game," he said. "We were punished a lot in key actions."

Divots, howlers and bad decisions - dissecting Man Utd's draw in Lisbon

Four goals, chaos and controversy - Man Utd held in Lisbon

Pochettino searching for first Man Utd win

Not for the first time this season, United controlled extended periods of a game they ended up not winning.

The goals they conceded at the Jose Alvalade were bizarre.

Seventy-five seconds after superbly saving one penalty, goalkeeper Lammens suffered a rush of blood and conceded another, which was scored.

Lammens was at fault for the second, when he dropped the ball into the path of Sporting striker Luis Suarez, who scored with an overhead kick.

"I think we dominated and we deserved to win the game, but we didn't for different circumstances," he said.

"All the teams make mistakes, but for these mistakes the punishment (for us) is too big in every single mistake. Many other clubs make mistakes or tilt in a different circumstance, in a more positive way. But that is in the way we are. We need to take responsibility."

United are still to win away from home in any competition this season. They have now won once in their last 13 matches. In the Champions League, they are 19th, two points in front of Roma, who are just below the top 24, which guarantees passage to the next phase.

Young said Lammens may be one mistake from being dropped.

The Belgian's performance was not good and errors are beginning to mount.

It is not what Pochettino needs right now. United showed faith in the Belgium international this summer by bringing in 36-year-old Karl Darlow as his understudy.

Darlow did end last season as first choice at Leeds but started just 30 league games in his three seasons with the Elland Road club. Tom Heaton, 40, who was also on the bench against Sporting, has not played in a senior game since February 2023.

Could Pochettino contemplate leaving Lammens out.

"This type of thing happens," he said. "That is football. Football is about making mistakes.

"I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.

"It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. We need to manage his type of situation better."

It has been a whirlwind week for Pochettino, who last Wednesday morning UK time was still United States boss.

There have been a few blows to absorb, and lessons are having to be learned quickly.

But despite the clear frustrations, the 54-year-old is glad he accepted the challenge.

"I am happy to be here," he said. "I'm so excited to be the face representing this club.

"We are here because the situation wasn't the situation all the fans and people expect. We are here to take the responsibility from one week, and we are going to improve for sure.

"It's going to be tough, of course. Nothing is easy. But we have the energy and I think we have the capacity, and, most important, we have the players and the power and the energy from our fans, which is massive."

articles.title: Miami’s Malachi Toney gets good news ahead of regular season finale vs. Boston College
articles.summary: Heading into their regular season finale against the visiting Boston College Eagles, the Miami football program will look to cap off another strong campaign...
articles.body:
Heading into their regular season finale against the visiting Boston College Eagles, the Miami football program will look to cap off another strong campaign at 11-1. A win would also give the Hurricanes more momentum heading into the final ACC Championship Game against Wake Forest. Miami also received another big boost, courtesy of head coach Mario Cristobal. According to college football insider Pete Nakos on X (formerly Twitter), Cristobal shared news that star wide receiver Malachi Toney is "probably a week and a half" away from making his return following a high ankle sprain and subsequent surgery.

"More positive news on Miami star WR Malachi Toney: Listed as doubtful for the regular-season finale against Boston College," Nakos reported. "ACC title game could be a feasible return. Mario Cristobal said last Friday he was 'probably a week and a half away.'"

Toney injured his ankle ahead of the Hurricanes' high-stakes tilt at Notre Dame in early November. Now, if Miami can get Toney back for the ACC title matchup against the Demon Deacons, it will give their chances a strong boost. Wake Forest's offense, under a transfer quarterback of their own in Gio Lopez, has been excellent as well. If the Hurricanes want to keep up, having Toney back on the field would be an equalizer.

Nevertheless, Miami must not overlook Boston College this weekend. With a win, the Eagles would become bowl eligible. For a program that has struggled to stay above .500 in the recent past, a bowl appearance would be a boon for Boston College. Still, Miami's offense should have plenty of firepower to keep the Eagles in check. Quarterback Darian Mensah continues to showcase why he's one of the nation's best signal callers. If he gets Toney back in time for the Wake Forest matchup, watch out Demon Deacons fans.

articles.title: Lobos running backs Scottre Humphrey, Kiefer Sibley questionable to play against Air Force
articles.summary: The Lobos might miss their two leading rushers against Air Force. New Mexico running backs Scottre Humphrey and Kiefer Sibley are listed as questionable for...
articles.body:
The Lobos might miss their two leading rushers against Air Force.

New Mexico running backs Scottre Humphrey and Kiefer Sibley are listed as questionable for Friday's regular season finale against the Falcons, per an availability report published by the Mountain West on Wednesday.

Humphrey has rushed for a team-high 762 yards and 14 touchdowns this season, his second with the Lobos. Sibley has rushed for 695 yards and five touchdowns after transferring in from North Texas this offseason.

Both Humphrey and Sibley are dealing with ankle injuries, per head coach Jason Eck. The former left UNM's 24-17 win at Wyoming on Friday in the first quarter with a sprained ankle and did not return.

Monday, Eck said Humphrey was scheduled to receive an MRI that night.

"I don't think he's ruled out, but I wouldn't say he's ruled in. either," he added. "So we'll have to see how he feels and what this MRI shows."

Sibley suffered what Eck called a "freak" ankle injury in UNM's last practice before playing Wyoming. Despite being listed as questionable, he notched a season-high 20 carries and rushed for 79 yards to lead the Lobos on the ground.

Sibley's fourth-and-1 touchdown run in the third quarter served as the game-winning touchdown against the Cowboys.

"He (sprained) his ankle in (Thursday's) practice, you know, he was in a boot on the plane," Eck said. "We didn't know if he was gonna play. He does warmups (and) comes out of warmups at 75%, 80% … Then Scottre sprains his ankle (on his) second carry, and (Sibley's) gotta go."

Safety Austin Brawley, tight end Tripp Walsh and offensive lineman Jaymar Tasi were also listed as questionable for Friday's game.

Linebacker Jaxton Eck (shoulder) is set to miss his seventh straight game despite gradually returning to practice activities. The fourth-year senior has not played since UNM's 61-7 win over UTEP on Oct. 3.

"We'll see about Jaxton," Eck said Monday. "We're still working through that."

A second availability report will be released in the hours before Saturday's game. All Mountain West teams are required to submit availability reports with designations, but without injury specifics, prior to each league contest.
